title.zh: 卷一百八十九下 列傳第一百三十九下: 儒學下
title.raw: 卷一百八十九下 列傳第一百三十九下: 儒學下 Volume 189 Biographies 139: Confucian Scholars 2

sentences.zh: 邢文偉，滁州全椒人也。

translations.literal: Xing Wenwei was a man of Quanjiao in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Wenwei came from Quanjiao in Chuzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少與和州高子貢、壽州裴懷貴俱以博學知名於江、淮間。

translations.literal: In youth, together with Gao Zigong of Hezhou and Pei Huaigui of Shouzhou, he was all famed for broad learning between the Yangtze and the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he, together with Gao Zigong of Hezhou and Pei Huaigui of Shouzhou, were renowned throughout the Yangtze–Huai region for their erudition.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，累遷太子典膳丞。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era, he was repeatedly promoted to Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianheng period (670–674) he rose through several posts to become Supervisor of the Crown Prince's Provisions.

sentences.zh: 時孝敬在東宮，罕與宮臣接見，文偉輒減膳，上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time Xiaojing was in the Eastern Palace and rarely received audiences with palace officials; Wenwei thereupon reduced his provisions and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Xiaojing was in the Eastern Palace and seldom met with his palace staff. Wenwei accordingly curtailed his own rations and submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣竊見《禮·戴記》曰：「太子既冠成人，免於保傅之嚴，則有司過之史，徹膳之宰。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen in the Liji, Daiji, it states: 'When the crown prince has been capped and become an adult, exempt from the strictness of guardian and tutor, then there is the historiographer who records faults and the steward who withdraws provisions.'
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject has noted what the Record of Rites (Dai Gong's record) says: 'Once the crown prince has received the cap and become an adult, freed from the strict oversight of his tutors, there shall be a historiographer to record his faults and a steward to withdraw his meals.'"

sentences.zh: 史之義，不得不司過；

translations.literal: The meaning of the historiographer is that he cannot but record faults;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer's duty is to record faults without fail;

sentences.zh: 宰之義，不得不徹膳，不徹膳則死。

translations.literal: the meaning of the steward is that he cannot but withdraw provisions—if he does not withdraw provisions, he dies.
translations.idiomatic: and the steward's duty is to withdraw meals without fail—if he fails to withdraw them, he must die."

sentences.zh: 」今皇帝式稽前典，妙簡英俊，自庶子已下，至諮議、舍人及學士、侍讀等，使翼佐殿下，以成聖德。

translations.literal: Now the Emperor has followed the former canon and finely selected outstanding men, from the Junior Tutor downward to Advisers, Gentlemen-in-Attendance, Academicians, and Lecturers, to assist Your Highness in completing sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor has now followed ancient precedent and carefully chosen outstanding men—from the junior tutors down through advisers, gentlemen-in-attendance, academicians, and lecturers—to assist Your Highness in cultivating sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 近日已來，未甚延納，談議不狎，謁見尚稀，三朝之後，但與內人獨居，何由發揮聖智，使睿哲文明者乎？

translations.literal: In recent days you have not greatly extended reception; discussion is not intimate, and audiences remain few. After the third audience of the day you dwell alone with inner attendants—how can sagely wisdom be brought forth and keen intelligence made manifest?
translations.idiomatic: Of late, however, Your Highness has not been very receptive: conversation lacks familiarity, and audiences remain infrequent. After the third audience of the day you keep only to your inner attendants—how then can sagely wisdom be brought forth and keen intelligence made manifest?

sentences.zh: 今史雖闕官，宰當奉職，忝備所司，未敢逃死，謹守禮經，輒申減膳。

translations.literal: Now though the historiographer's post is vacant, the steward ought to perform his duty. I am unworthy in the office I hold and dare not flee death; reverently observing the ritual canon, I venture to announce my reduction of provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Though the historiographer's post is now vacant, the steward must still perform his duty. I am unworthy of the office I hold, yet I dare not shirk the penalty of death prescribed by ritual; reverently following the canon, I hereby announce that I am curtailing my provisions.

sentences.zh: 太子答書曰：

translations.literal: The crown prince replied in a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied in a letter:

sentences.zh: 顧以庸虛，早尚墳典，每欲研精政術，極意書林。

translations.literal: Considering my mediocrity and emptiness, I early honored the classics of the tombs and always wished to refine my mastery of statecraft and devote myself utterly to the forest of books.
translations.idiomatic: Aware of my own mediocrity, I have long revered the classical canon and have always wished to refine my grasp of statecraft and devote myself fully to study.

sentences.zh: 但往在幼年，未閑將衛，竭誠耽誦，因即損心。

translations.literal: But formerly in my youth I was unversed in guard and escort; I devoted myself wholeheartedly to recitation and thereby harmed my heart.
translations.idiomatic: But in my youth, unaccustomed to the rigors of guard duty, I threw myself wholeheartedly into study and thereby damaged my health.

sentences.zh: 比日以來，風虛更積，中奉恩旨，不許重勞。

translations.literal: In recent days wind-deficiency has accumulated further; I have received the gracious decree in the palace forbidding heavy exertion.
translations.idiomatic: Lately my chronic weakness has grown worse, and I have received an imperial decree forbidding me to overexert myself.

sentences.zh: 加以趨侍含元，溫清朝夕，承親以無專之道，遵禮以色養為先。

translations.literal: Moreover I attend at Hanyuan morning and evening in clear warmth, receiving my parent with the Way of non-partiality and observing ritual by putting nourishing through demeanor first.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I attend the emperor at Hanyuan Palace morning and evening, serving my parent without partiality and observing ritual by giving priority to caring for him through proper demeanor.

sentences.zh: 所以屢闕坐朝，時乖學緒。

translations.literal: Therefore I have repeatedly missed sitting court and at times fallen short in the thread of study.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason I have often been absent from court audiences and have sometimes neglected my studies.

sentences.zh: 公潛申勖戒，聿薦忠規，敬尋來請，良符宿誌。

translations.literal: You, sir, have secretly offered admonition and encouragement and presented loyal counsel; respectfully reviewing your request, it well accords with my long-held resolve.
translations.idiomatic: You have discreetly offered encouragement and presented loyal counsel; on carefully reviewing your request, I find it accords well with my long-held resolve.

sentences.zh: 自非情思審諭，義均弼諧，豈能進此藥言，形於簡墨！

translations.literal: Had it not been for careful understanding in feeling and thought and righteousness equal to assisting harmony, how could you have advanced this healing counsel and set it down in writing!
translations.idiomatic: Had you not understood my situation so clearly and offered counsel worthy of a true minister, how could you have ventured such salutary advice and set it down in writing!

sentences.zh: 撫躬三省，感愧兼深！

translations.literal: Touching my person and reflecting thrice, I am moved and ashamed in equal depth!
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on myself again and again, I am deeply moved and ashamed!

sentences.zh: 文偉自是益知名。

translations.literal: From this Wenwei became still more renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From this incident Wenwei's reputation grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 其後右史缺官，高宗謂侍臣曰：「邢文偉事我兒，能減膳切諫，此正直人也。

translations.literal: Later the post of Right Historiographer was vacant; Gaozong said to attending ministers: 'Xing Wenwei served my son and was able to reduce his provisions and offer earnest remonstrance—this is an upright man.'
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the post of Right Historiographer fell vacant, Emperor Gaozong told his attending ministers: "Xing Wenwei served my son and was willing to curtail his own rations and offer earnest remonstrance—he is an upright man."

sentences.zh: 」遂擢拜右史。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted and appointed Right Historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly promoted to Right Historiographer.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，累遷鳳閣侍郎，兼弘文館學士。

translations.literal: When Zetian held court, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and concurrently Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu held court, he rose through several posts to Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and concurrently served as an Academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 載初元年，遷內史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zaichu he was transferred to Inner Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: In 689 he was appointed Inner Scribe.

sentences.zh: 天授初，內史宗秦客以奸贓獲罪，文偉坐附會秦客，貶授珍州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianshou, Inner Scribe Zong Qinke was convicted of corruption; Wenwei was implicated for associating with Qinke and demoted to Prefect of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianshou era (690), Inner Scribe Zong Qinke was convicted of corruption; Wenwei was implicated for associating with Qinke and demoted to prefect of Zhen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後有制使至其州境，文偉以為殺己，遽自縊而死。

translations.literal: Later when an imperial commissioner reached the border of his prefecture, Wenwei thought he had come to kill him and immediately hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an imperial commissioner arrived at the border of his prefecture, Wenwei believed he had been sent to execute him and immediately hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 高子貢者，和州歷陽人也。

translations.literal: Gao Zigong was a man of Liyang in Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zigong came from Liyang in Hezhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弱冠遊太學，遍涉《六經》，尤精《史記》。

translations.literal: At the capping age he studied at the Imperial Academy, traversing all the Six Classics and especially mastering the Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he entered the Imperial Academy, studied all six classics, and was especially accomplished in the Records of the Grand Historian.

sentences.zh: 與文偉及亳州硃敬則為莫逆之交。

translations.literal: With Wenwei and Zhu Jingze of Bozhou he formed bonds of inseparable friendship.
translations.idiomatic: He formed the closest of friendships with Wenwei and Zhu Jingze of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 明經舉，歷秘書正字、弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: Recommended in the Mingjing examination, he served successively as Proofreader of the Secretariat and Direct Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the Mingjing examination he served as proofreader of the Secretariat and direct academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 郁郁不得誌，棄官而歸。

translations.literal: Depressed and unable to fulfill his ambitions, he abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Frustrated in his ambitions, he resigned his post and returned home.

sentences.zh: 屬徐敬業作亂於揚州，遣弟敬猷統兵五千人，緣江西上，將逼和州。

translations.literal: When Xu Jingye raised rebellion at Yangzhou, he sent his younger brother Jingyou to command five thousand troops, advancing up the west bank of the river, about to press upon Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingye rebelled at Yangzhou, he sent his younger brother Jingyou with five thousand troops up the west bank of the Yangtze, threatening to advance on Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 子貢率鄉曲數百人拒之，自是賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: Zigong led several hundred local men to resist them; from this the rebels did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: Zigong led several hundred local men to resist them, and from then on the rebels did not dare attack the area.

sentences.zh: 以功擢授朝散大夫，拜成均助教。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted and granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and appointed Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and appointed assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 虢王鳳之子東莞公融，曾為和州刺史，從子貢受業，情義特深。

translations.literal: Prince of Guo Feng's son, Duke of Dongguan Rong, had once been Prefect of Hezhou and studied under Zigong; their bond of feeling was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, Duke of Dongguan, son of Prince Feng of Guo, had once served as prefect of Hezhou and had studied under Zigong; their bond was especially close.

sentences.zh: 及融為申州，陰懷異志。

translations.literal: When Rong was at Shenzhou he secretly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was posted to Shen prefecture, he secretly harbored rebellious ambitions.

sentences.zh: 令黃公撰結交於子貢，推為謀主。

translations.literal: He had Huang Gongzhuan befriend Zigong and promoted him as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: He had Huang Gongzhuan cultivate Zigong's friendship and made him chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 潛謀密議，書信往復，諸王內外相應，皆出自其策。

translations.literal: They plotted in secret and exchanged letters back and forth; the princes within and without responded to one another—all stemming from his stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted in secret and exchanged letters; the princes coordinated their actions inside and outside the capital—all according to his plans.

sentences.zh: 尋而事發，被誅。

translations.literal: Before long the affair was exposed and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the plot was exposed and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 郎余令，定州新樂人也。

translations.literal: Lang Yuling was a man of Xinle in Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Yuling came from Xinle in Dingzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖楚之，少與兄蔚之，俱有重名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chuzhi, in youth together with his elder brother Weizhi, both had great renown.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chuzhi and Chuzhi's elder brother Weizhi both enjoyed great renown in their youth.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，蔚之為左丞，楚之為尚書民曹郎。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui, Weizhi was Left Vice Director and Chuzhi was Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign of Sui (605–618), Weizhi served as left vice director and Chuzhi as gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 煬帝重其兄弟，稱為二郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang valued the brothers and called them the Two Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang held the brothers in high regard and called them "the Two Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 楚之，武德初為大理卿，與太子少保李綱、侍中陳叔達撰定律令。

translations.literal: Chuzhi, at the beginning of Wude was Minister of Justice and, together with Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Li Gang and Attendant-in-Chief Chen Shuda, drafted statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wude reign (618), Chuzhi served as minister of justice and, together with Junior Tutor Li Gang and Attendant-in-Chief Chen Shuda, drafted the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 後受詔招諭山東，為竇建德所獲，脅以兵刃，又誘以厚利，楚之竟不為屈。

translations.literal: Later he received an edict to summon and instruct Shandong and was captured by Dou Jiande, who threatened him with weapons and also enticed him with rich profit, yet Chuzhi in the end would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was ordered to win over the eastern provinces and was captured by Dou Jiande, who threatened him with arms and tempted him with rich rewards, yet Chuzhi refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 及還，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: When he returned, on account of old age he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he retired from office on account of his age.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，卒，時年八十。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Zhenguan reign, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 余令父知運，貝州刺史；

translations.literal: Yuling's father Zhiyun was Prefect of Bei;
translations.idiomatic: Yuling's father Zhiyun served as prefect of Bei prefecture;

sentences.zh: 兄余慶，高宗時萬年令，理有威名，京城路不拾遺，後卒於交州都督。

translations.literal: his elder brother Yuqing, in Gaozong's time was Magistrate of Wannian, governing with a reputation for awe; in the capital no one picked up what others dropped on the road; he later died as Military Governor of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: his elder brother Yuqing, who under Emperor Gaozong served as magistrate of Wannian with such authority that lost property was left untouched in the capital streets, and who later died while serving as military governor of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 余令少以博學知名，舉進士。

translations.literal: Yuling in youth was famed for broad learning and was recommended in the Jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yuling was known from youth for his erudition and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 初授霍王元軌府參軍，數上詞賦，元軌深禮之。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Military Adjutant in the household of Prince Huo Yuan Gui, repeatedly submitted rhapsodies and fu, and Yuan Gui treated him with deep respect.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed military adjutant in the household of Prince Huo Yuan Gui, submitted several literary compositions, and was treated with great respect by the prince.

sentences.zh: 先是，余令從父知年為霍王友，亦見推仰。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuling's father's younger cousin Zhinian had been Friend to Prince Huo and was also esteemed and admired.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuling's father's younger cousin Zhinian had served as friend to Prince Huo and was likewise held in high regard.

sentences.zh: 元軌謂人曰：「郎氏兩賢，人之望也。

translations.literal: Yuan Gui said to others: 'The two worthy men of the Lang clan are what people look to.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Gui remarked to others: "These two worthy men of the Lang clan are the hope of us all."

sentences.zh: 相次入府，不意培塿而松柏成林。

translations.literal: They entered the household in succession—I did not expect a mound to become a forest of pine and cypress.
translations.idiomatic: They have entered my household one after another—I never expected a mere mound to grow into a forest of pine and cypress."

sentences.zh: 」轉幽州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Recording Secretary of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to recording secretary of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有客僧聚眾欲自焚，長史裴照率官屬欲往觀之。

translations.literal: At the time a visiting monk gathered a crowd intending self-immolation; Chief Administrator Pei Zhao led subordinate officials wishing to go observe.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a visiting monk gathered a crowd intending to burn himself alive; Chief Administrator Pei Zhao led his subordinates to go and watch.

sentences.zh: 余令曰：「好生惡死，人之性也。

translations.literal: Yuling said: 'Loving life and hating death is human nature.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuling said: "Love of life and hatred of death are human nature."

sentences.zh: 違越教義，不近人情。

translations.literal: To violate and transgress religious teaching is not close to human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: To violate religious teaching in this way is contrary to human nature.

sentences.zh: 明公佐守重籓，須察其奸詐，豈得輕舉，觀此妖妄！

translations.literal: Your Excellency assists in guarding a great frontier— you must investigate his deceit; how can you lightly go to watch this demonic delusion!
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency assists in governing an important frontier post—you must investigate his deception. How can you lightly go to witness such demonic folly!"

sentences.zh: 」照從其言，因收僧按問，果得詐狀。

translations.literal: Zhao followed his words, thereupon seized the monk and interrogated him, and indeed obtained proof of fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao followed his advice, arrested the monk, and interrogated him—and indeed uncovered the fraud.

sentences.zh: 孝敬在東宮，余令續梁元帝《孝德傳》，撰《孝子後傳》三十卷，以獻，甚見嗟重。

translations.literal: When Xiaojing was in the Eastern Palace, Yuling continued Emperor Yuan of Liang's Biographies of Filial Virtue and compiled Later Biographies of Filial Sons in thirty juan, presenting them as tribute; he was greatly admired and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xiaojing was in the Eastern Palace, Yuling continued Emperor Yuan of Liang's Biographies of Filial Virtue and compiled Later Biographies of Filial Sons in thirty juan, which he presented to the crown prince and was greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 累轉著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Assistant in the Bureau of Authorship.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to assistant in the Bureau of Authorship.

sentences.zh: 撰《隋書》未成，會病卒，時人甚痛惜之。

translations.literal: He was compiling the Book of Sui but had not finished when he fell ill and died; people of the time deeply grieved and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He was compiling the Book of Sui but had not finished when he fell ill and died; contemporaries deeply mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 路敬淳，貝州臨清人也。

translations.literal: Lu Jingchun was a man of Linqing in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingchun came from Linqing in Bei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父文逸。

translations.literal: His father was Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，闔門遇盜，文逸潛匿草澤，晝伏於死人中，夜行避難。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui Daye, the whole household encountered bandits; Wenyi hid secretly in marshes and grass, by day lying among the dead, by night traveling to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui Daye reign, the entire family fell victim to bandits; Wenyi hid in the marshes, lying among the dead by day and traveling by night to escape.

sentences.zh: 自傷窮梗，閉口不食。

translations.literal: Grieving his destitution and hardship, he closed his mouth and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving his destitution, he refused all food.

sentences.zh: 同侶閔其謹願，勸以不當滅性，捃拾以食之，遞負之而行，遂免於難。

translations.literal: His companions pitied his earnest sincerity, urged that he ought not destroy his nature, gathered food and fed him, took turns carrying him as they went, and thus he escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: His companions, pitying his earnest nature, urged him not to destroy himself, gathered food for him, took turns carrying him on their journey, and thus he escaped danger.

sentences.zh: 貞觀末，官至申州司馬。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguan he reached the post of Vice Administrator of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Zhenguan reign he had risen to vice administrator of Shen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 敬淳與季弟敬潛俱早知名。

translations.literal: Jingchun and his youngest younger brother Jingqian were both early renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun and his youngest brother Jingqian were both known from an early age.

sentences.zh: 敬淳尤勤學，不窺門庭，遍覽墳籍，而孝友篤敬。

translations.literal: Jingchun was especially diligent in study, never glancing beyond the gate and courtyard, reading through all the classics of the tombs, and was filial, friendly, and deeply reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun was especially diligent in study, never leaving his gate, reading widely in the classical canon, and was deeply filial and devoted to his friends.

sentences.zh: 遭喪，三年不出廬寢。

translations.literal: When he encountered bereavement, for three years he did not leave the mourning hut.
translations.idiomatic: When his parent died, he did not leave the mourning hut for three years.

sentences.zh: 服免，方號慟入見其妻，形容羸毀，妻不之識也。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, only then did he wail and go in to see his wife; his appearance was emaciated and ruined, and his wife did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he went in wailing to see his wife; he was so emaciated that she did not recognize him.

sentences.zh: 後舉進士。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended in the Jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 天授中，歷司禮博士、太子司議郎，兼修國史，仍授崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: In Tianshou he served successively as Erudite of the Ministry of Rites, Secretary for Discussion of the Crown Prince, concurrently compiling the National History, and was also granted Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he served as erudite of the Ministry of Rites and secretary for discussion of the crown prince, concurrently compiled the national history, and was appointed academician of the Chongxian Hall.

sentences.zh: 數受詔修緝吉兇雜儀，則天深重之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received edicts to compile and edit auspicious, inauspicious, and miscellaneous rites; Zetian deeply valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He received repeated edicts to compile rites for auspicious and inauspicious occasions; Empress Wu held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天二年，坐與綦連耀結交，下獄死。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian, on account of associating with Qi Lianyao, he was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: In 697 he was imprisoned and died on account of his association with Qi Lianyao.

sentences.zh: 敬淳尤明譜學，盡能究其根源枝派，近代已來，無及之者。

translations.literal: Jingchun was especially expert in genealogy, fully able to trace roots and branches; in recent times there has been none to equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchun was especially expert in genealogy and could trace every clan to its roots and branches; in recent times none could match him.

sentences.zh: 撰《著姓略記》十卷，行於時。

translations.literal: He compiled Brief Records of Distinguished Surnames in ten juan, which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Brief Records of Distinguished Surnames in ten juan, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 又撰《衣冠本系》，未成而死。

translations.literal: He also compiled Origins of the Gentry but died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: He also began Origins of the Gentry but died before completing it.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，追贈秘書少監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong reign (705) he was posthumously granted vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敬潛仕至中書舍人。

translations.literal: Jingqian in office reached Gentleman of the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqian rose to gentleman of the Secretariat Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 王元感，濮州鄄城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yuangan was a man of Juancheng in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuangan came from Juancheng in Pu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少舉明經，累補博城縣丞。

translations.literal: In youth he was recommended in the Mingjing examination and was repeatedly appointed Assistant Magistrate of Bocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he passed the Mingjing examination and was repeatedly appointed assistant magistrate of Bocheng county.

sentences.zh: 兗州都督、紀王慎深禮之，命其子東平王續從元感受學。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Yanzhou, Prince of Ji Shen, treated him with deep respect and ordered his son, Prince of Dongping Xu, to study under Yuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shen of Ji, military governor of Yanzhou, treated him with great respect and had his son Xu, Prince of Dongping, study under Yuangan.

sentences.zh: 天授中，稍遷左衛率府錄事，兼直弘文館。

translations.literal: In Tianshou he was gradually promoted to Recording Secretary of the Left Guard Command and concurrently served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was gradually promoted to recording secretary of the Left Guard Command and concurrently served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 是後則天親祠南郊及享明堂，封嵩嶽，元感皆受詔共諸儒撰定儀註，凡所立議，眾鹹推服之。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Zetian personally sacrificed at the Southern Altar and offered at the Bright Hall, and enfeoffed Mount Song, Yuangan each time received edicts together with the various Confucians to draft and fix ritual commentaries; whatever proposals he made, the multitude all deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when Empress Wu personally sacrificed at the Southern Altar, offered at the Bright Hall, and enfeoffed Mount Song, Yuangan received edicts on each occasion to draft ritual regulations together with other scholars; whatever he proposed, all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 轉四門博士，仍直弘文館。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Four Gates and still served on duty at the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to erudite of the Four Gates and continued to serve on duty at the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 元感時雖年老，猶能燭下看書，通宵不寐。

translations.literal: Although Yuangan was by then old in years, he could still read by lamplight and go the whole night without sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, he could still read by lamplight through the entire night without sleep.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，表上其所撰《尚書糾謬》十卷、《春秋振滯》二十卷、《禮記繩愆》三十卷，並所註《孝經》、《史記》稿草，請官給紙筆，寫上秘書閣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an he memorialized and presented his compositions: Correcting Errors in the Documents in ten juan, Reviving Stagnation in the Spring and Autumn in twenty juan, Binding Faults in the Record of Rites in thirty juan, together with draft commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Shiji, requesting that the government supply paper and brush to copy them up to the Secretariat Archive.
translations.idiomatic: In 703 he submitted memorials presenting his works: Correcting Errors in the Documents (ten juan), Reviving Stagnation in the Spring and Autumn (twenty juan), and Binding Faults in the Record of Rites (thirty juan), together with draft commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Records of the Grand Historian, requesting official paper and brush to have them copied into the Secretariat archive.

sentences.zh: 詔令弘文、崇賢兩館學士及成均博士詳其可否。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the academicians of the Hongwen and Chongxian halls and the erudites of the Directorate of Education to examine in detail whether they were acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the academicians of the Hongwen and Chongxian halls and the erudites of the Directorate of Education to evaluate their merits.

sentences.zh: 學士祝欽明、郭山惲、李憲等皆專守先儒章句，深譏元感掎摭舊義，元感隨方應答，竟不之屈。

translations.literal: Academicians Zhu Qinming, Guo Shanyun, Li Xian, and others all clung exclusively to the chapter-and-phrase of former Confucians and deeply criticized Yuangan for plucking and gathering old meanings; Yuangan answered according to each point and in the end was not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: The academicians Zhu Qinming, Guo Shanyun, Li Xian, and others, who clung exclusively to traditional commentaries, sharply criticized Yuangan for departing from established interpretations; Yuangan answered each objection point by point and was not defeated.

sentences.zh: 鳳閣舍人魏知古、司封郎中徐堅、左史劉知幾、右史張思敬，雅好異聞，每為元感申理其義，連表薦之。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Phoenix Pavilion Wei Zhigu, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Rites Xu Jian, Left Historiographer Liu Zhiji, and Right Historiographer Zhang Sijing, who elegantly loved unusual learning, each time explained and justified Yuangan's meanings and submitted successive memorials recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu, gentleman of the Phoenix Pavilion; Xu Jian, bureau director of the Ministry of Rites; Liu Zhiji, left historiographer; and Zhang Sijing, right historiographer—all lovers of innovative scholarship—repeatedly defended Yuangan's interpretations and submitted successive memorials recommending him.

sentences.zh: 尋下詔曰：「王元感質性溫敏，博聞強記，手不釋卷，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was issued, saying: 'Wang Yuangan's nature is gentle and keen, broadly learned with a powerful memory; his hand never releases a scroll, and in old age he is still more devoted.'
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict was issued: "Wang Yuangan is gentle and keen by nature, broadly learned with a powerful memory; his hand never leaves his books, and in old age his devotion grows only stronger.

sentences.zh: 掎前達之失，究先聖之旨，是謂儒宗，不可多得。

translations.literal: He plucks the errors of former worthies and exhausts the aims of the former sages—this is what is called a patriarch of Confucian learning, not to be obtained in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: He corrects the errors of earlier scholars and penetrates the intentions of the ancient sages—he is a true patriarch of Confucian learning, and such men are rare.

sentences.zh: 可太子司議郎，兼崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: He may be made Secretary for Discussion of the Crown Prince and concurrently Academician of the Chongxian Hall.'
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him Secretary for Discussion of the Crown Prince and concurrently Academician of the Chongxian Hall."

sentences.zh: 」魏知古嘗稱其所撰書曰：「信可謂《五經》之指南也。

translations.literal: Wei Zhigu once praised the books he had composed, saying: 'They may truly be called a compass for the Five Classics.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhigu once praised his writings, saying: "They may truly serve as a compass for the Five Classics."

sentences.zh: 」中宗即位，以春宮舊僚，進加朝散大夫，拜崇賢館學士。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, as a former colleague from the Eastern Palace he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and appointed Academician of the Chongxian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Yuangan was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and appointed academician of the Chongxian Hall as a former colleague from the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 王紹宗，揚州江都人也，梁左民尚書銓曾孫也，其先自瑯邪徙焉。

translations.literal: Wang Shaozong was a man of Jiangdu in Yangzhou, great-great-grandson of Quan, Minister of the Left Household of Liang; his ancestors had moved there from Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaozong came from Jiangdu in Yangzhou prefecture. He was the great-great-grandson of Quan, Minister of the Left Household of Liang; his ancestors had migrated there from Langya.

sentences.zh: 紹宗少勤學，遍覽經史，尤工草隸。

translations.literal: Shaozong in youth was diligent in study, reading through the classics and histories, and was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shaozong studied diligently, read widely in the classics and histories, and was especially accomplished in cursive and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 家貧，常傭力寫佛經以自給，每月自支錢足即止，雖高價盈倍，亦即拒之。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he often hired out his labor copying Buddhist sutras to support himself. Each month when the money he allotted himself was sufficient he would stop, and even if offered prices many times higher he would refuse.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor, and he often supported himself by copying Buddhist sutras for hire. Each month he stopped work once he had earned enough for his needs, and even when offered many times his usual rate he refused.

sentences.zh: 寓居寺中，以清凈自守，垂三十年。

translations.literal: He lodged in a monastery and kept himself in purity and quiet, for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a monastery and maintained a life of purity and seclusion for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 文明中，徐敬業於揚州作亂，聞其高行，遣使征之，紹宗稱疾固辭。

translations.literal: In the Wenming era, when Xu Jingye raised rebellion at Yangzhou, hearing of his lofty conduct he sent envoys to summon him; Shaozong pleaded illness and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wenming era, when Xu Jingye rebelled at Yangzhou, he heard of Shaozong's exemplary conduct and sent envoys to summon him; Shaozong pleaded illness and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 又令唐之奇親詣所居逼之，竟不起。

translations.literal: He also had Tang Zhiqi go in person to his dwelling to press him, but in the end he would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Tang Zhiqi in person to his dwelling to compel him, but Shaozong still refused to go.

sentences.zh: 敬業大怒，將殺之。

translations.literal: Jingye was greatly enraged and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingye was furious and was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 之奇曰：「紹宗人望，殺之恐傷士眾之心。

translations.literal: Zhiqi said: 'Shaozong is the hope of the people; to kill him would likely wound the hearts of scholars and the masses.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhiqi said: "Shaozong enjoys the esteem of the people; killing him would likely alienate scholars and the masses."

sentences.zh: 」由是獲免。

translations.literal: By this he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he was spared.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，行軍大總管李孝逸以其狀聞，則天驛召赴東都，引入禁中，親加慰撫，擢拜太子文學，累轉秘書少監，仍侍皇太子讀書。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Grand General on Campaign Li Xiaoyi reported his situation; Zetian summoned him by post horse to the Eastern Capital, brought him into the inner palace, personally comforted and encouraged him, promoted him to Literary Scholar of the Crown Prince, repeatedly transferred him to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and still attended the crown prince in reading.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was suppressed, Grand General Li Xiaoyi reported his conduct to the court; Empress Wu summoned him by imperial courier to the Eastern Capital, received him in the inner palace, personally comforted him, appointed him literary scholar to the crown prince, later promoted him to vice director of the Secretariat, and had him continue to attend the crown prince in his studies.

sentences.zh: 紹宗性淡雅，以儒素見稱，當時朝廷之士，鹹敬慕之。

translations.literal: Shaozong's nature was refined and plain; he was praised for Confucian simplicity, and the gentlemen of the court at the time all admired and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong was refined and unpretentious by nature and was admired for his scholarly simplicity; court officials of the day all held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 張易之兄弟，亦加厚禮。

translations.literal: The brothers Zhang Yizhi also treated him with added courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Zhang Yizhi also treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 易之伏誅，紹宗坐以交往見廢，卒於鄉里。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, Shaozong was implicated for association and dismissed from office; he died in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yizhi was executed, Shaozong was dismissed from office for his association with him and died in his home district.

sentences.zh: 韋叔夏，尚書左僕射安石兄也。

translations.literal: Wei Shuxia was the elder brother of Anshi, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuxia was the elder brother of Anshi, left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 少而精通《三禮》。

translations.literal: From youth he thoroughly mastered the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he thoroughly mastered the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 其叔父太子詹事琨嘗謂曰：「汝能如是，可以繼丞相業矣！

translations.literal: His father's younger brother, Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Kun, once said to him: 'If you can be like this, you may succeed to the chancellor's enterprise!'
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Kun, grand mentor of the crown prince, once told him: "If you can achieve such mastery, you may succeed to the chancellor's legacy!"

sentences.zh: 」舉明經。

translations.literal: He was recommended in the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 調露年，累除太常博士。

translations.literal: In the Diaolu year he was repeatedly appointed Erudite of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 679 he was appointed erudite of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 後屬高宗崩，山陵舊儀多廢缺，叔夏與中書舍人賈太隱、太常博士裴守貞等，草創撰定，由是授春官員外郎。

translations.literal: Later when Gaozong died, the old rites for the imperial tomb were largely abandoned and deficient; Shuxia, together with Gentleman of the Secretariat Jia Taiyin, Erudite of the Ministry of Rites Pei Shouzhen, and others, drafted and fixed them anew, and thereby he was granted Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong died, many of the old rites for the imperial tomb had fallen into disuse; Shuxia, together with Jia Taiyin, gentleman of the Secretariat, Pei Shouzhen, erudite of the Ministry of Rites, and others, drafted and established new regulations, and was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 則天將拜洛及享明堂，皆別受制，共當時大儒祝欽明、郭山惲撰定儀註。

translations.literal: When Zetian was about to perform the feng rite at Luo and offer at the Bright Hall, she each time received separate edicts and, together with the great Confucians of the time Zhu Qinming and Guo Shanyun, drafted and fixed ritual commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu performed the feng rite at Luoyang and offered at the Bright Hall, she received separate edicts on each occasion and, together with the leading scholars Zhu Qinming and Guo Shanyun, drafted ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 凡所立議，眾鹹推服之。

translations.literal: Whatever proposals he made, the multitude all deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he proposed, all deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 累遷成均司業。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 久視元年，特下制曰：「吉兇禮儀，國家所重，司禮博士，未甚詳明。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiushi a special edict was issued, saying: 'Auspicious and inauspicious ritual observances are what the state values; the erudites of the Ministry of Rites are not very clear and thorough.'
translations.idiomatic: In 700 a special edict was issued: "Rites for auspicious and inauspicious occasions are matters of great state importance, yet the erudites of the Ministry of Rites are not sufficiently versed in them.

sentences.zh: 成均司業韋叔夏、太子率更令祝欽明等，博涉禮經，多所該練，委以參掌，冀弘典式。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Directorate of Education Wei Shuxia, Commandant of the Crown Prince's Rate Bureau Zhu Qinming, and others are broadly versed in the ritual canon and thoroughly accomplished in many areas—entrust them with joint administration, hoping to expand canonical models.'
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuxia, vice director of the Directorate of Education, Zhu Qinming, commandant of the crown prince's rate bureau, and others are broadly versed in the ritual canon—entrust them with this task in the hope of expanding our canonical models.

sentences.zh: 自今司禮所修儀註，並委叔夏等刊定訖，然後進奏。」

translations.literal: From now on, whatever ritual commentaries the Ministry of Rites compiles shall all be entrusted to Shuxia and others to revise and fix, and only then submitted for imperial review.'
translations.idiomatic: From now on, all ritual regulations compiled by the Ministry of Rites shall be entrusted to Shuxia and others for revision before submission to the throne."

sentences.zh: 長安四年，擢春官侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chang'an he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 704 he was promoted to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，轉太常少卿，充建立廟社使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites and served as Commissioner for Establishing the Ancestral Temple and Altars of Soil and Grain.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong reign he was transferred to vice minister of rites and appointed commissioner for establishing the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 以功進銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 累封沛國郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒時年七十余。

translations.literal: When he died he was over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over seventy years of age.

sentences.zh: 撰《五禮要記》三十卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled Essential Records of the Five Rites in thirty juan, which circulated in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Essential Records of the Five Rites in thirty juan, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 贈兗州都督、修文館學士，謚曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Military Governor of Yanzhou and Academician of the Xiuxian Hall; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of military governor of Yanzhou and academician of the Xiuxian Hall, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 子縚，太常卿。

translations.literal: His son Tao was Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao served as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 祝欽明，雍州始平人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Qinming was a man of Shiping in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qinming came from Shiping in Yongzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少通《五經》，兼涉眾史百家之說。

translations.literal: From youth he mastered the Five Classics and also ranged through the various histories and the teachings of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he mastered the Five Classics and also studied widely in history and the teachings of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 舉明經。

translations.literal: He was recommended in the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 長安元年，累遷太子率更令，兼崇文館學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chang'an he was repeatedly promoted to Commandant of the Crown Prince's Rate Bureau and concurrently Academician of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In 701 he rose to commandant of the crown prince's rate bureau and concurrently served as academician of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 中宗在春宮，欽明兼充侍讀。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace, Qinming also served as Lecturer-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong was crown prince, Qinming also served as his lecturer-in-attendance.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，中宗將親祀南郊，欽明與國子司業郭山惲二人奏言皇后亦合助祭，遂建議曰：

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, when Zhongzong was about to sacrifice personally at the Southern Altar, Qinming and Vice Director of the National University Guo Shanyun submitted that the empress should also assist in the sacrifice, and thereupon presented a proposal, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In 709, when Emperor Zhongzong was about to sacrifice personally at the Southern Altar, Qinming and Guo Shanyun, vice director of the National University, submitted that the empress should also assist in the sacrifice and presented the following proposal:

sentences.zh: 謹按《周禮》，天神曰祀，地祇曰祭，宗廟曰享。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the Zhouli: the celestial spirit is called si, the earthly spirit is called ji, and the ancestral temple is called xiang.
translations.idiomatic: "According to the Rites of Zhou, sacrifices to celestial spirits are called si, those to earthly spirits ji, and those at the ancestral temple xiang.

sentences.zh: 大宗伯職曰：「祀大神，祭大祇，享大鬼，理其大禮。

translations.literal: The office of the Grand Minister of Rites states: 'Sacrifice to the great spirit, offer to the great earthly spirit, present to the great ghost, and regulate their great rites.'
translations.idiomatic: The office of the Grand Minister of Rites states: 'Sacrifice to the great celestial spirit, offer to the great earthly spirit, present offerings to the great ancestral spirits, and regulate their great rites.'

sentences.zh: 若王有故不預，則攝位。

translations.literal: If the king has cause and does not attend, then another takes his place in proxy.
translations.idiomatic: If the king has cause and cannot attend, another takes his place in proxy.

sentences.zh: 凡大祭祀，王後不預，則攝而薦豆籩，徹。

translations.literal: For all great sacrifices, if the queen does not attend, then she takes proxy and presents the dou and bian vessels, and withdraws them.
translations.idiomatic: For all great sacrifices, if the queen does not attend, she takes proxy and presents and withdraws the dou and bian vessels.

sentences.zh: 」又追師職：「掌王後之首服，以待祭祀。

translations.literal: Further, the office of the Chief Seamstress states: 'She manages the queen's headgear, to await sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the office of the Chief Seamstress states: 'She manages the queen's ceremonial headgear in preparation for sacrifices.'

sentences.zh: 」又內司服職：「掌王後之六服。

translations.literal: Further, the office of the Inner Director of Garments states: 'She manages the queen's six garments.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the office of the Inner Director of Garments states: 'She manages the queen's six ceremonial garments.'

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，供後之衣服。

translations.literal: For all sacrifices she supplies the queen's garments.
translations.idiomatic: For all sacrifices she supplies the queen's garments.

sentences.zh: 」又九嬪職：「大祭祀，後稞獻則贊，瑤爵亦如之。

translations.literal: Further, the office of the Nine Consorts states: 'At great sacrifices, when the queen performs the kuo offering she assists, and likewise for the jade libation cup.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the office of the Nine Consorts states: 'At great sacrifices, when the queen performs the kuo offering she assists, and likewise for the jade libation cup.'

sentences.zh: 」據此諸文，即皇后合助皇帝祀天神、祭地祇，明矣。

translations.literal: According to these passages, it is clear that the empress should assist the emperor in sacrificing to the celestial spirit and offering to the earthly spirit.
translations.idiomatic: From these passages it is clear that the empress should assist the emperor in sacrificing to celestial spirits and offering to earthly spirits.

sentences.zh: 故鄭玄註《內司服》云：「闕狄，皇后助王祭群小祀之服。

translations.literal: Therefore Zheng Xuan annotates the Inner Director of Garments, saying: 'Que di is the garment by which the queen assists the king in sacrificing at all minor rites.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Inner Director of Garments states: 'The que di is the garment the queen wears when assisting the king at minor sacrifices.'

sentences.zh: 」然則小祀尚助王祭，中、大推理可知。

translations.literal: Thus even at minor sacrifices she still assists the king in sacrifice; for medium and great sacrifices the inference by reasoning is knowable.
translations.idiomatic: If she assists at minor sacrifices, it follows by inference that she does so at medium and great sacrifices as well.

sentences.zh: 闕狄之上，猶有兩服：第一祎衣，第二搖狄，第三闕狄。

translations.literal: Above the que di there are still two garments: first the yi garment, second the yao di, third the que di.
translations.idiomatic: Above the que di are two further garments: first the yi garment, second the yao di, and third the que di.

sentences.zh: 此三狄，皆助祭之服。

translations.literal: These three di are all garments for assisting in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: These three di garments are all worn when assisting in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 闕狄即助祭小祀，即知搖狄助祭中祀，祎衣助祭大祀。

translations.literal: The que di assists at minor sacrifices; thus one knows the yao di assists at medium sacrifices and the yi garment assists at great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The que di is worn at minor sacrifices; it follows that the yao di is worn at medium sacrifices and the yi garment at great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 鄭舉一隅，故不委說。

translations.literal: Zheng cited one corner and therefore did not explain fully.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng cited only one example and therefore did not explain the matter fully.

sentences.zh: 唯祭宗廟，《周禮》王有兩服，先王袞冕，先公柷冕。

translations.literal: Only for sacrificing at the ancestral temple—in the Zhouli the king has two garments: for former kings the gun and mian, for former lords the zhu and mian.
translations.idiomatic: Only for sacrifices at the ancestral temple does the Zhouli prescribe two garments for the king: the gun and mian for former kings, the zhu and mian for former lords.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄因此以後助祭宗廟，亦分兩服，云：「祎衣助祭先王，搖狄助祭先公。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan therefore held that when the queen assists in sacrificing at the ancestral temple, she also divides into two garments, saying: 'The yi garment assists in sacrificing to former kings; the yao di assists in sacrificing to former lords.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan therefore held that when the queen assists at ancestral temple sacrifices she also wears two garments, saying: 'The yi garment is worn when sacrificing to former kings; the yao di when sacrificing to former lords.'

sentences.zh: 」不言助祭天地社稷，自宜三隅而反。

translations.literal: He did not speak of assisting in sacrificing to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain; by the rule of three corners one may infer in reverse.
translations.idiomatic: He did not mention assisting at sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain; by the rule of inferring the whole from one part, the conclusion follows.

sentences.zh: 且《周禮》正文：「凡祭，王後不預。

translations.literal: Moreover the main text of the Zhouli states: 'For all sacrifices, if the queen does not attend.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the main text of the Zhouli states: 'For all sacrifices, if the queen does not attend—'

sentences.zh: 」既不專言宗廟，即知兼祀天地，故云「凡」也。

translations.literal: Since it does not speak exclusively of the ancestral temple, one knows it includes sacrificing to Heaven and Earth; therefore it says 'all.'
translations.idiomatic: Since it does not speak exclusively of the ancestral temple, it clearly includes sacrifices to Heaven and Earth; hence the word 'all.'

sentences.zh: 又《春秋外傳》云：「禘郊之事，天子親射其牲，王後親舂其粢。

translations.literal: Further, the Outer Commentary on the Spring and Autumn states: 'At the di and jiao rites, the Son of Heaven personally shoots the sacrificial animal; the queen personally pounds the sacrificial grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the Outer Commentary on the Spring and Autumn states: 'At the di and jiao rites, the Son of Heaven personally shoots the sacrificial animal, and the queen personally pounds the sacrificial grain.'

sentences.zh: 」故代婦職但云：「詔王後之禮事」，不主言宗廟也。

translations.literal: Therefore the office of the Chief Matron only says 'instruct the queen in ritual affairs' and does not chiefly speak of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the office of the Chief Matron speaks only of 'instructing the queen in ritual affairs' and does not refer chiefly to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 若專主宗廟者，則內宗、外宗職皆言「掌宗廟之祭祀」。

translations.literal: If it chiefly concerned the ancestral temple, then the offices of the Inner and Outer Ancestral Managers would all say 'manage sacrifices at the ancestral temple.'
translations.idiomatic: If it concerned only the ancestral temple, the offices of the Inner and Outer Ancestral Managers would say 'manage sacrifices at the ancestral temple.'

sentences.zh: 此皆禮文分明，不合疑惑。

translations.literal: These ritual texts are all clear and distinct; there should be no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: These ritual texts are all perfectly clear and admit of no doubt.

sentences.zh: 舊說以天子父天、母地、兄日、姊月，所以祀天於南郊，祭地於北郊，朝日於東門之外，以昭事神，訓人事，君必躬親以禮之，有故然後使攝，此其義也。

translations.literal: The old teaching holds that the Son of Heaven takes Heaven as father, Earth as mother, the sun as elder brother, and the moon as elder sister; therefore he sacrifices to Heaven at the Southern Altar, offers to Earth at the Northern Altar, and attends the sun outside the eastern gate—to make manifest service to the spirits and instruct human affairs. The ruler must personally perform the rites; only when there is cause does he then have another take proxy—this is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: According to traditional teaching, the Son of Heaven regards Heaven as his father, Earth as his mother, the sun as his elder brother, and the moon as his elder sister. He therefore sacrifices to Heaven at the Southern Altar, offers to Earth at the Northern Altar, and attends the sun outside the eastern gate—to manifest service to the spirits and instruct human affairs. The ruler must personally perform these rites; only when prevented does he have another act in his place. Such is the meaning.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·祭統》曰：「夫祭也者，必夫婦親之，所以備內外之官也。

translations.literal: The Liji, Jitong, states: 'Sacrifice must be performed by husband and wife together, in order to complete the offices of inner and outer.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites (Jitong) states: 'Sacrifice must be performed by husband and wife together, in order to complete the offices of inner and outer.'

sentences.zh: 官備則具備。

translations.literal: When the offices are complete, the offering is complete.
translations.idiomatic: When the offices are complete, the offering is complete.

sentences.zh: 」又，「哀公問於孔子曰：『冕而親迎，不已重乎？

translations.literal: Further: 'Duke Ai asked Confucius, saying: "To wear the cap and go in person to welcome the bride—is this not excessive?"'
translations.idiomatic: Further: 'Duke Ai asked Confucius: "To wear the ceremonial cap and go in person to welcome the bride—is this not excessive?"'

sentences.zh: 』孔子愀然作色而對曰：『合二姓之好，以繼先聖之後，以為天地宗廟社稷之主，君何謂已重焉！

translations.literal: Confucius changed expression and answered, saying: "To unite the good of two surnames, to continue the descendants of former sages, and to become master of the altars of Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain—how can Your Lordship call this excessive!"'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's expression changed as he replied: "To unite two clans in marriage, to continue the line of former sages, and to become master of the altars of Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain—how can Your Lordship call this excessive!"'

sentences.zh: 』」又《漢書·郊祀志》云：「天地合祭，先祖配天，先妣配地。

translations.literal: Further, the Hanshu, Jiaosi zhi, states: 'Heaven and Earth are sacrificed to together; the former ancestors are paired with Heaven, the former consorts with Earth.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices in the Book of Han states: 'Heaven and Earth are sacrificed to together; the former ancestors are paired with Heaven, the former consorts with Earth.'

sentences.zh: 天地合精，夫婦判合。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth unite their essences; husband and wife are paired in union.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth unite their essences; husband and wife are joined in union.

sentences.zh: 祭天南郊，則以地配，一體之義也。

translations.literal: When sacrificing to Heaven at the Southern Altar, Earth is paired with it—the meaning of a single body.
translations.idiomatic: When sacrificing to Heaven at the Southern Altar, Earth is paired with it—the meaning of their unity as one body.

sentences.zh: 」據此諸文，即知皇后合助祭，望請別修助祭儀註同進。

translations.literal: According to these passages, one knows the empress should assist in sacrifice; we respectfully request that separate ritual commentaries for assisting sacrifice be drafted and submitted together.
translations.idiomatic: From these passages it is clear that the empress should assist in sacrifice; we respectfully request that separate ritual regulations for her assistance be drafted and submitted together.

sentences.zh: 帝頗以為疑，召禮官親問之。

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat doubtful and summoned the ritual officials to question them in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was somewhat doubtful and summoned the ritual officials to question them in person.

sentences.zh: 太常博士唐紹、蔣欽緒對曰：「皇后南郊助祭，於禮不合。

translations.literal: Erudites of the Ministry of Rites Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu replied: 'For the empress to assist in sacrifice at the Southern Altar is not in accord with ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: The erudites Tang Shao and Jiang Qinxu replied: "For the empress to assist in sacrifice at the Southern Altar is not in accord with ritual."

sentences.zh: 但欽明所執，是祭宗廟禮，非祭天地禮。

translations.literal: But what Qinming holds to is the ritual for sacrificing at the ancestral temple, not the ritual for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: What Qinming cites, however, concerns sacrifices at the ancestral temple, not sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 謹按魏、晉、宋及齊、梁、周、隋等歷代史籍，至於郊天祀地，並無皇后助祭之事。

translations.literal: Respectfully according to the historical records of Wei, Jin, Song, and Qi, Liang, Zhou, Sui, and other dynasties, as for suburban sacrifice to Heaven and offering to Earth, there is nowhere any instance of the empress assisting in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: According to the historical records of Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Zhou, Sui, and other dynasties, nowhere is there any instance of an empress assisting at suburban sacrifices to Heaven or offerings to Earth.

sentences.zh: 」帝令宰相取兩家狀對定。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chancellors to take the memorials of both sides and determine the matter by comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chancellors to compare the memorials of both sides and decide the matter.

sentences.zh: 欽緒與唐紹及太常博士彭景直又奏議曰：

translations.literal: Qinxu, together with Tang Shao and Erudite of the Ministry of Rites Peng Jingzhi, again submitted a memorial for deliberation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qinxu, together with Tang Shao and the erudite Peng Jingzhi, submitted a further memorial for deliberation:

sentences.zh: 《周禮》凡言祭、祀、享三者，皆祭之互名，本無定義。

translations.literal: In the Zhouli, wherever ji, si, and xiang are spoken of, all three are interchangeable names for sacrifice and originally have no fixed definition.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou, the terms ji, si, and xiang are interchangeable names for sacrifice and originally have no fixed definition.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How may this be made clear?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be demonstrated?

sentences.zh: 按《周禮》典瑞職云：「兩珪有邸，以祀地。

translations.literal: According to the Zhouli, office of the Director of Regalia: 'Two gui with bases, to si the earth.'
translations.idiomatic: The office of the Director of Regalia in the Rites of Zhou states: 'Two gui with bases, to sacrifice to the earth.'

sentences.zh: 」則祭地亦稱祀也。

translations.literal: Thus offering to Earth is also called si.
translations.idiomatic: Thus offerings to Earth are also called si.

sentences.zh: 又司筵云：「設祀先王之胙席。

translations.literal: Further, the Director of Mats says: 'Set out the si mats for the former kings' sacrificial portions.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the Director of Mats says: 'Set out the sacrificial mats for the former kings' portions.'

sentences.zh: 」則祭宗廟亦稱祀也。

translations.literal: Thus sacrificing at the ancestral temple is also called si.
translations.idiomatic: Thus sacrifices at the ancestral temple are also called si.

sentences.zh: 又內宗職云：「掌宗廟之祭祀。

translations.literal: Further, the office of the Inner Ancestral Manager says: 'Manage sacrifices at the ancestral temple.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the office of the Inner Ancestral Manager says: 'Manage sacrifices at the ancestral temple.'

sentences.zh: 」此又非獨天稱祀，地稱祭也。

translations.literal: This again is not that only Heaven is called si and Earth is called ji.
translations.idiomatic: This again shows that Heaven alone is not called si and Earth alone ji.

sentences.zh: 又按《禮記》云：「惟聖為能享帝。

translations.literal: Further, according to the Liji: 'Only the sage can xiang the Lord on High.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the Record of Rites states: 'Only the sage can present offerings to the Lord on High.'

sentences.zh: 」此即祀天帝亦言享也。

translations.literal: This shows that sacrificing to the Lord of Heaven is also called xiang.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that sacrifices to the Lord of Heaven are also called xiang.

sentences.zh: 又按《孝經》云：「春秋祭祀，以時思之。

translations.literal: Further, according to the Xiaojing: 'In spring and autumn perform ji and si, thinking of them at the proper seasons.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the Classic of Filial Piety states: 'In spring and autumn perform sacrifices, remembering them at the proper seasons.'

sentences.zh: 」此即宗廟亦言祭祀也。

translations.literal: This shows that the ancestral temple is also spoken of as ji and si.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the ancestral temple is also spoken of with the terms ji and si.

sentences.zh: 經典此文，不可備數。

translations.literal: Such passages in the classics cannot be fully enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: Such passages in the classics are too numerous to cite in full.

sentences.zh: 據此則欽明所執天曰祀，地曰祭，廟曰享，未得為定，明矣！

translations.literal: According to this, Qinming's holding that Heaven is called si, Earth ji, and the temple xiang cannot be established as fixed—it is clear!
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that Qinming's claim that Heaven is called si, Earth ji, and the temple xiang cannot be established as fixed!

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》凡言大祭祀者，祭天地宗廟之總名，不獨天地為大祭也。

translations.literal: Further, in the Zhouli wherever 'great sacrifice' is spoken of, it is the general name for sacrificing to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple—not that Heaven and Earth alone are the great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Further, in the Rites of Zhou wherever 'great sacrifice' is mentioned, it is a general term for sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple—not that Heaven and Earth alone constitute the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How may this be made clear?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be demonstrated?

sentences.zh: 按《爵人職》云：「大祭祀，與量人授舉斝之卒爵。

translations.literal: According to the office of the Cupbearer: 'At great sacrifices, together with the Measurer he presents the final cup of the raised jia.'
translations.idiomatic: The office of the Cupbearer states: 'At great sacrifices, together with the Measurer he presents the final cup of the raised jia.'

sentences.zh: 」屍與斝，皆宗廟之事，則宗廟亦稱大祭祀。

translations.literal: The corpse and the jia are both matters of the ancestral temple; thus the ancestral temple is also called a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The corpse and the jia cup are both matters of the ancestral temple; thus the ancestral temple is also called a great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 又欽明狀引九嬪職：「大祭祀，後稞獻則贊瑤爵。

translations.literal: Further, Qinming's memorial cites the office of the Nine Consorts: 'At great sacrifices, when the queen performs the kuo offering she assists with the jade cup.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, Qinming's memorial cites the office of the Nine Consorts: 'At great sacrifices, when the queen performs the kuo offering she assists with the jade cup.'

sentences.zh: 」據祭天無稞，亦無瑤爵，此乃宗廟稱大祭祀之明文。

translations.literal: According to this, in sacrificing to Heaven there is no kuo and no jade cup—this is explicit text that the ancestral temple is called a great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Since sacrifices to Heaven involve neither the kuo offering nor the jade cup, this is explicit evidence that 'great sacrifice' refers to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 欽明所執大祭祀即為祭天地，未得為定，明矣！

translations.literal: Qinming's holding that great sacrifice means sacrificing to Heaven and Earth cannot be established as fixed—it is clear!
translations.idiomatic: Qinming's claim that 'great sacrifice' means sacrifices to Heaven and Earth cannot be established—it is clear!

sentences.zh: 又《周禮》大宗伯職云：「凡大祭祀，王後有故不預，則攝而薦豆籩，徹。

translations.literal: Further, the Zhouli, office of the Grand Minister of Rites, states: 'For all great sacrifices, if the queen has cause and does not attend, then she takes proxy and presents the dou and bian vessels and withdraws them.'
translations.idiomatic: Further, the office of the Grand Minister of Rites in the Rites of Zhou states: 'For all great sacrifices, if the queen has cause and does not attend, she takes proxy and presents and withdraws the dou and bian vessels.'

sentences.zh: 」欽明唯執此文，以為王後有祭天地之禮。

translations.literal: Qin Ming clung solely to this passage, holding that the queen consort had the rite of sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Ming seized on this passage alone, insisting that the queen was entitled to perform the rites of sacrifice to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 欽緒等據此，乃是王後薦宗廟之禮，非祭天地之事。

translations.literal: Qin Xu and the others relied on this, [arguing] that it was the queen's rite of presenting offerings at the ancestral temple, not a matter of sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xu and his colleagues cited the same text to show that it described the queen's presentation of offerings in the ancestral temple—not any ceremony directed at Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How is this to be demonstrated?
translations.idiomatic: How may this be proved?

sentences.zh: 按此文：「凡祀大神，祭大祇，享大鬼，帥執事而卜日宿，視滌濯，蒞玉鬯，省牲鑊，奉玉齏，詔大號，理其大禮，詔相王之大禮。

translations.literal: Examining this text: 'In all cases of sacrificing to the Great Spirit, offering to the Great Earth Lord, and feasting the Great Ghosts, [one] leads the officers to divine the day and lodge [there], inspects the cleansing and washing, attends to the jade and fragrant wine, examines the sacrificial vessels and cauldrons, presents the jade and finely chopped meat, announces the great titles, arranges the great rites, and is charged to assist the king in his great rites.'
translations.idiomatic: Consider the passage itself: 'Whenever one sacrifices to the Great Spirit, offers to the Great Earth Lord, and feasts the Great Ghosts, one leads the officers to choose the day by divination and keep the vigil, oversees the purifications, attends to the jade and the fragrant libation, inspects the cauldrons and the sacrificial meat, presents the jade and the minced offering, proclaims the great titles, sets in order the great ceremonies, and is appointed to assist the king in the great rites.'

sentences.zh: 若王不與祭祀，則攝位。

translations.literal: If the king does not participate in the sacrifice, then [one] assumes his place.
translations.idiomatic: If the king does not attend the sacrifice, another stands in his stead.

sentences.zh: 」此已上一「凡」，直是王兼祭天地宗廟之事，故通言大神、大祇、大鬼之祭也。

translations.literal: The 'in all cases' above directly concerns the king's joint performance of sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple; hence it speaks generally of sacrifices to the Great Spirit, the Great Earth Lord, and the Great Ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: That first 'whenever' plainly covers the king's combined duties in the rites of Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temple—which is why it speaks broadly of offerings to the Great Spirit, the Great Earth Lord, and the Great Ghosts.

sentences.zh: 已下文云：「凡大祭祀，王後不與，則攝而薦豆籩，徹。

translations.literal: The text below states: 'In all great sacrifices, if the queen consort does not participate, then [one] assumes [her role] and presents the dou and bian vessels, and performs the removal.'
translations.idiomatic: The passage that follows reads: 'In every great sacrifice, if the queen does not attend, another stands in for her to present the dou and bian vessels and perform the withdrawal.'

sentences.zh: 」此一「凡」，直是王後祭廟之事，故唯言大祭祀也。

translations.literal: This 'in all cases' directly concerns the queen's temple sacrifices; hence it speaks only of great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: That second 'whenever' refers only to the queen's rites in the temple—which is why it mentions great sacrifices and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 若雲王後助祭天地，不應重起「凡大祭祀」之文也。

translations.literal: If one were to say the queen assists in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, one should not again introduce the phrase 'in all great sacrifices.'
translations.idiomatic: If the queen truly assisted in the rites of Heaven and Earth, the text would not need to open a fresh section with 'in every great sacrifice.'

sentences.zh: 為嫌王後有祭天地之疑，故重起後「凡」以別之耳。

translations.literal: Because of suspicion that the queen had rites for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth, [the text] deliberately begins again with 'in all cases' afterward to distinguish them—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The later 'whenever' was added precisely to dispel any suspicion that the queen shared in the rites of Heaven and Earth—to mark the distinction, and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 王後祭廟，自是大祭祀，何故取上「凡」相王之禮，以混下「凡」王後祭宗廟之文？

translations.literal: The queen's sacrifice at the temple is itself a great sacrifice—why take the earlier 'in all cases' concerning rites assisting the king and conflate it with the later 'in all cases' concerning the queen's sacrifice at the ancestral temple?
translations.idiomatic: The queen's temple rites are already 'great sacrifices' in their own right—so why borrow the earlier 'whenever,' which governs assisting the king, and use it to blur the later 'whenever,' which governs the queen's offerings in the ancestral temple?

sentences.zh: 此是本經科段明白。

translations.literal: This is clearly the division of sections in the original classic.
translations.idiomatic: The original text itself draws the section break with perfect clarity.

sentences.zh: 又按《周禮》：「外宗掌宗廟之祭祀，佐王後薦玉豆。

translations.literal: Furthermore, according to the Rites of Zhou: 'The Outer Chancellors manage sacrifices at the ancestral temple and assist the queen in presenting jade and dou vessels.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou likewise states: 'The Outer Chancellors oversee the ancestral temple sacrifices and assist the queen in presenting the jade and the dou vessels.'

sentences.zh: 凡後之獻，亦如之。

translations.literal: In all presentations by the queen, they likewise assist.
translations.idiomatic: In every offering made by the queen, they serve in the same capacity.

sentences.zh: 王後有故不預，則宗伯攝而薦豆籩。

translations.literal: If the queen has some impediment and does not attend, then the Director of Ritual assumes [her role] and presents the dou and bian vessels.
translations.idiomatic: If the queen is prevented from attending, the Director of Ritual stands in for her and presents the dou and bian vessels.

sentences.zh: 」外宗無佐祭天地之禮。

translations.literal: The Outer Chancellors have no rite of assisting in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Outer Chancellors have no office in the rites of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 但天地尚質，宗廟尚文。

translations.literal: But Heaven and Earth favor simplicity; the ancestral temple favors ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth demand plainness; the ancestral temple demands refinement.

sentences.zh: 玉豆，宗廟之器，初非祭天所設。

translations.literal: Jade and dou vessels are implements of the ancestral temple—they were never established for sacrifices to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jade and the dou vessel belong to the temple ritual—they were never ordained for the sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 請問欽明，若王後助祭天地，在《周禮》使何人贊佐？

translations.literal: I ask Qin Ming: if the queen assists in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, whom does the Rites of Zhou appoint to assist?
translations.idiomatic: Tell us, Qin Ming: if the queen were to assist in the rites of Heaven and Earth, whom does the Rites of Zhou assign to assist her?

sentences.zh: 若宗伯攝後薦豆祭天，又合何人贊佐？

translations.literal: If the Director of Ritual, assuming the queen's role, presents dou vessels in a sacrifice to Heaven, who then should assist?
translations.idiomatic: And if the Director of Ritual, standing in for the queen, were to present the dou vessels at a sacrifice to Heaven, who would assist him?

sentences.zh: 並請明征禮文，即知攝薦是宗廟之禮明矣。

translations.literal: Please clearly cite the ritual texts on both points, and it will be evident that assuming [her role] to present offerings is clearly a rite of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Cite the ritual texts on both counts, and it will at once be plain that standing in to present offerings belongs to the temple rite—not to the rites of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 按《周禮·司服》云：「王祀昊天上帝，則服大裘而冕。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, Director of Garments: 'When the king sacrifices to the August Heaven and Supreme Lord, he wears the great fur robe and cap.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, in the chapter on the Director of Garments, says: 'When the king sacrifices to August Heaven and the Supreme Lord, he wears the great fur robe and the royal cap.'

sentences.zh: 享先王，則袞冕。

translations.literal: When he feasts the former kings, he wears the robe with twelve symbols and cap.
translations.idiomatic: When he offers to the former kings, he wears the twelve-symbol robe and cap.

sentences.zh: 」內司服，「掌王後祭服」，無王後祭天之服。

translations.literal: The Inner Director of Garments 'manages the queen's sacrificial garments'—there are no garments for the queen's sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Director of Garments 'presides over the queen's sacrificial dress'—yet no garment is prescribed for the queen's sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 按《三禮義宗》明王後六服，謂祎衣、搖翟、闕翟、鞠衣、展衣、褖衣。

translations.literal: According to the Exposition of the Three Rites, the queen's six garments are named: the yi robe, the swaying pheasant, the truncated pheasant, the curled robe, the display robe, and the bordered robe.
translations.idiomatic: The Exposition of the Three Rites lists the queen's six ceremonial robes: the yi robe, the swaying-pheasant robe, the truncated-pheasant robe, the curled robe, the display robe, and the bordered robe.

sentences.zh: 「祎衣從王祭先王則服之，搖翟祭先公及饗諸侯則服之，鞠衣以采桑則服之，展衣以禮見王及見賓客則服之，褖衣燕居服之。

translations.literal: 'The yi robe is worn when following the king to sacrifice to former kings; the swaying pheasant when sacrificing to former lords and feasting the feudal lords; the curled robe when gathering mulberry leaves; the display robe when paying ceremonial visits to the king and receiving guests; the bordered robe for leisurely residence.'
translations.idiomatic: 'She wears the yi robe when she follows the king to sacrifice to the former kings; the swaying-pheasant robe when sacrificing to former lords or feasting the feudal lords; the curled robe when gathering mulberry leaves; the display robe for formal audiences with the king or with guests; and the bordered robe for repose at leisure.'

sentences.zh: 」王後無助祭於天地之服，但自先王已下。

translations.literal: The queen has no garments for assisting in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth—only from former kings downward.
translations.idiomatic: The queen possesses no vestments for assisting in the rites of Heaven and Earth—only those used from the former kings downward.

sentences.zh: 又《三禮義宗》明後夫人之服云：「後不助祭天地五嶽，故無助天地四望之服。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Exposition of the Three Rites clarifies the queen consort's garments, stating: 'The queen does not assist in sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the Five Sacred Peaks, hence she has no garments for assisting at sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the Four Quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: The Exposition of the Three Rites also defines the queen consort's dress, saying: 'The queen does not assist in sacrifices to Heaven, Earth, and the Five Sacred Peaks, and therefore has no robes for assisting at the rites of Heaven, Earth, and the Four Quarters.'

sentences.zh: 」按此，則王後無祭天之服，明矣。

translations.literal: From this, it is clear that the queen has no garments for sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On this evidence alone, it is clear that the queen has no robe for sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《三禮義宗》明王後五輅，謂重翟、厭翟、安車、翟車、輦車也。

translations.literal: The Exposition of the Three Rites clarifies the queen's five chariots: the heavy pheasant, the subdued pheasant, the comfortable carriage, the pheasant carriage, and the palanquin.
