translations.idiomatic: The Exposition of the Three Rites likewise defines the queen's five carriages: the Heavy Pheasant, the Subdued Pheasant, the Comfort Carriage, the Pheasant Carriage, and the Palanquin.

sentences.zh: 「重翟者，後從王祭先王、先公所乘也；

translations.literal: 'The heavy pheasant is what the queen rides when following the king to sacrifice to former kings and lords;'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Heavy Pheasant is the carriage the queen uses when she follows the king to sacrifice to the former kings and lords;'

sentences.zh: 厭翟者，後從王饗諸侯所乘也；

translations.literal: 'the subdued pheasant is what she rides when following the king to feast the feudal lords;'
translations.idiomatic: 'the Subdued Pheasant, when she follows the king to feast the feudal lords;'

sentences.zh: 安車者，後宮中朝夕見於王所乘也；

translations.literal: 'the comfortable carriage is what she rides when seeing the king morning and evening within the palace;'
translations.idiomatic: 'the Comfort Carriage, for her morning and evening audiences with the king within the inner palace;'

sentences.zh: 翟車者，後求桑所乘也；

translations.literal: 'the pheasant carriage is what she rides when gathering mulberry leaves;'
translations.idiomatic: 'the Pheasant Carriage, when she goes to gather mulberry leaves;'

sentences.zh: 輦車者，後遊宴所乘也。

translations.literal: 'the palanquin is what she rides for outings and banquets.'
translations.idiomatic: 'and the Palanquin, for outings and banquets.'

sentences.zh: 」按此，則王後無祭天之車明矣。

translations.literal: From this, it is likewise clear that the queen has no chariot for sacrificing to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: By the same logic, it is equally clear that the queen has no carriage ordained for sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 又《禮記·郊特牲·義贊》云：「祭天無稞。

translations.literal: Furthermore, the Exposition on the Record of Rites, 'Special Sacrifices at the Suburbs,' states: 'In sacrifices to Heaven there is no kuo.'
translations.idiomatic: The Exposition on the Record of Rites, in 'Special Sacrifices at the Suburbs,' also says: 'In the sacrifice to Heaven there is no kuo offering.'

sentences.zh: 鄭玄註云：『唯人道宗廟有稞。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary states: 'Only in human rites at the ancestral temple is there kuo.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments: 'Only in the human rites of the ancestral temple is the kuo performed.'

sentences.zh: 天地大神，至尊不稞。

translations.literal: Heaven and Earth, the supreme spirits—being most exalted, there is no kuo.'
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth, being the supreme powers, are too august to receive the kuo.'

sentences.zh: 』圓丘之祭，與宗廟不同。

translations.literal: The sacrifice at the Round Mound differs from that at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Round Mound sacrifice and the ancestral temple rite are not the same.

sentences.zh: 朝踐，王酌泛齊以獻，是一獻。

translations.literal: At the morning audience and treading [on the blood], the king ladles out the diluted qi wine to present—it is the first presentation.
translations.idiomatic: At the morning audience and the treading rite, the king pours the diluted qi wine and presents it—this is the first offering.

sentences.zh: 後無祭天之事，大宗伯次酌醴齊以獻，是為二獻。

translations.literal: The queen has no role in sacrifices to Heaven; the Grand Director of Ritual next ladles out the li qi wine to present—this is the second presentation.
translations.idiomatic: The queen has no part in the sacrifice to Heaven; the Grand Director of Ritual next pours the li qi wine and presents it—this is the second offering.

sentences.zh: 」按此，則祭圓丘，大宗伯次王為獻，非攝王後之事。

translations.literal: From this, in the sacrifice at the Round Mound, the Grand Director of Ritual presents after the king—it is not a matter of assuming the queen's role.
translations.idiomatic: Thus at the Round Mound, the Grand Director of Ritual presents after the king—it is not a case of standing in for the queen.

sentences.zh: 欽明等所執王後有故不預，則宗伯攝薦豆籩，更明攝王後宗廟之薦，非攝天地之祀明矣。

translations.literal: What Qin Ming and his associates relied upon—'if the queen has some impediment and does not attend, then the Director of Ritual assumes [her role] and presents the dou and bian'—further clarifies that assuming [her role] to present offerings at the ancestral temple is meant, not assuming [her role] in sacrifices to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The very passage Qin Ming and his allies invoke—'if the queen is prevented from attending, the Director of Ritual stands in for her and presents the dou and bian'—makes it still clearer that such substitution governs the queen's temple offerings, not the rites of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 欽緒等幸忝禮官，親承聖問，竭盡聞見，不敢依隨。

translations.literal: Qin Xu and his colleagues, fortunate to serve as ritual officials and personally entrusted with the sage's inquiry, have exhausted their knowledge and dare not simply follow along.
translations.idiomatic: We of Qin Xu's party are humbled to serve as masters of ritual and to answer the Son of Heaven in person; having set forth all we know, we dare not fall in with the other view.

sentences.zh: 伏以主上稽古，誌遵舊典，所議助祭，實無明文。

translations.literal: We humbly observe that His Majesty examines antiquity and intends to follow the old statutes; as for the proposed assistance in sacrifice, there is truly no explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: We submit that Your Majesty, in consulting antiquity and seeking to uphold the ancient canon, will find no explicit authority for the queen's supposed assistance in sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 時尚書左僕射韋巨源又希旨，協同欽明之議。

translations.literal: At the time, Wei Juyuan, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, again sought to please [the throne] and collaborated with Qin Ming's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Juyuan, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, once again read the emperor's wishes and sided with Qin Ming.

sentences.zh: 上納其言，竟以後為亞獻，仍補大臣李嶠等女為齊娘，以執籩豆。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted their words, and in the end made the queen the secondary presenter, additionally appointing daughters of senior ministers such as Li Qiao as 'Qiniang' to hold the bian and dou vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took their counsel. In the end he made the queen the secondary presenter, and further appointed daughters of great ministers such as Li Qiao as ritual maidens called Qiniang, to bear the bian and dou vessels.

sentences.zh: 及禮畢，特詔齊娘有夫婿者，鹹為改官。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, a special edict was issued that Qiniang who had husbands would all have their husbands' ranks changed.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, a special edict declared that every Qiniang who already had a husband would see her husband promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，侍御史倪若水劾奏欽明及郭山惲曰：「欽明等本自腐儒，素無操行，崇班列爵，實為叨忝。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Jingyun era, Censor Ni Ruoshui memorialized impeaching Qin Ming and Guo Shanyun, stating: 'Qin Ming and his kind are fundamentally mere pedantic scholars, utterly devoid of moral conduct; their elevation to the court ranks and enfeoffment is truly an undeserved grace.'
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingyun reign, the Censor Ni Ruoshui submitted an impeachment of Qin Ming and Guo Shanyun, declaring: 'Men like Qin Ming are pedants to the core, men of no character whatever; that they were raised to court rank and granted noble titles was pure undeserved favor.'

sentences.zh: 而涓塵莫效，諂佞為能。

translations.literal: Yet not even a mote of dust was contributed; flattery and sycophancy were taken as ability.
translations.idiomatic: Yet none contributed even the least service; flattery and sycophancy alone passed for talent.

sentences.zh: 遂使曲臺之禮，圜丘之制，百王故事，一朝墜失。

translations.literal: Thus the rites of Quetai, the regulations of the Circular Mound, and the precedents of a hundred kings were lost in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the rites of Quetai, the institutions of the Circular Mound, and the precedents of a hundred kings—all fell away in a single day.

sentences.zh: 所謂亂常改作，希旨病君，人之不才，遂至於此。

translations.literal: What is called violating the constants and altering institutions, seeking to please [the ruler] while harming the ruler—men lacking ability have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by violating order and altering the rites, currying favor even while harming the sovereign—such is what incompetence leads to.

sentences.zh: 今聖明馭歷，賢良入用，惟茲小人，猶在朝列。

translations.literal: Now a sage and enlightened ruler holds the throne, the worthy and good enter office, yet these petty men still remain in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Now that a sage sovereign holds the throne and the worthy enter service, only these petty men still linger in the court ranks.

sentences.zh: 臣請並從黜放，以肅周行。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that they all be dismissed and banished together, to cleanse the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they all be dismissed together, to restore dignity to the court.

sentences.zh: 」於是左授欽明饒州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qin Ming was demoted to the left and appointed Prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Qin Ming was transferred to the lesser post of Prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 後入為崇文館學士。

translations.literal: Later he entered office as an academician of the Chongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was again appointed an academician of the Chongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 郭山惲，蒲州河東人。

translations.literal: Guo Shanyun was a native of Hedong in Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shanyun was from Hedong in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 少通《三禮》。

translations.literal: In youth he mastered the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was versed in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷國子司業。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era, he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong reign, he rose through successive promotions to Vice Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時中宗數引近臣及修文學士，與之宴集，嘗令各效伎藝，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhongzong frequently summoned close ministers and the literary scholars of the Xiucheng Hall to feast with him, and once ordered each to display his skills for amusement and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Zhongzong often summoned his close ministers and the literary scholars of the Xiucheng Hall to join him in feasts, and once had each display his talents for mirth and amusement.

sentences.zh: 工部尚書張錫為《談容娘舞》，將作大匠宗晉卿舞《渾脫》，左衛將軍張洽舞《黃麞》，左金吾衛將軍杜元琰誦《婆羅門咒〗》，給事中李行言唱《駕車西河》，中書舍人盧藏用效道士上章。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhang Xi performed the 'Dance of Tan Rongniang'; Master Builder Zong Jinqing danced the 'Huntuo'; General of the Left Guard Zhang Qia danced the 'Yellow Roebuck'; General of the Left Golden Raven Guard Du Yuanyan recited the 'Brahmin Imprecation'; Palace Attendant Li Xingyan sang 'Driving the Chariot to Xihe'; Palace Secretary Lu Zangyong mimicked a Daoist submitting a memorial to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Zhang Xi performed the Dance of Tan Rongniang; Master Builder Zong Jinqing danced the Huntuo; General of the Left Guard Zhang Qia danced the Yellow Roebuck; General of the Left Golden Raven Guard Du Yuanyan recited the Brahmin Imprecation; Palace Attendant Li Xingyan sang Driving the Chariot to Xihe; Palace Secretary Lu Zangyong impersonated a Daoist submitting a memorial to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 山惲獨奏曰：「臣無所解，請誦古詩兩篇。

translations.literal: Shanyun alone submitted: 'Your subject has no skill to display; I ask to recite two ancient poems.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyun alone stepped forward and said: 'Your humble servant has no skill to show; I beg leave to recite two ancient poems.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，於是誦《鹿鳴》、《蟋蟀》之詩。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented, and so he recited the poems 'The Cry of the Deer' and 'The Cricket.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and he recited the 'Deer Cry' and 'Cricket' from the Book of Songs.

sentences.zh: 奏未畢，中書令李嶠以其詞有「好樂無荒」之語，頗涉規諷，怒為忤旨，遽止之。

translations.literal: Before he finished, Chief Minister of the Secretariat Li Jiao, because the lines contained the phrase 'take pleasure without excess,' which seemed to offer remonstrance, angrily deemed it contrary to the imperial intent and abruptly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished, Li Jiao, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, noting that the lines contained the phrase 'take pleasure without excess'—which seemed a veiled remonstrance—flew into a rage at this breach of imperial intent and cut him short.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝嘉山惲之意，詔曰：「郭山惲業優經史，識貯古今，《八索》、《九丘》，由來遍覽；

translations.literal: The next day, the Emperor praised Shanyun's intent and issued an edict saying: 'Guo Shanyun's scholarship in the classics and histories is superior, his knowledge encompasses past and present, and from of old he has read widely in the Eight Indexes and Nine Mounds;
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor praised Shanyun's intent and issued an edict: 'Guo Shanyun's mastery of the classics and histories is outstanding, his learning spans past and present, and from of old he has read widely in the Eight Indexes and Nine Mounds;

sentences.zh: 前言往行，實所該詳。

translations.literal: Earlier words and past deeds—he is truly well versed in them all.
translations.idiomatic: The words of former ages and the deeds of past men—he is truly well versed in them all.

sentences.zh: 昨者因其豫遊，式宴朝彥，既乘歡洽，咸使詠歌。

translations.literal: Yesterday, on the occasion of his leisurely excursion and formal banquet for the court's eminent men, riding the tide of convivial joy, all were made to sing and recite.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday, at his leisurely outing and formal banquet for the court's eminent men, amid the warmth of shared delight, all were made to sing and recite.

sentences.zh: 遂能誌在匡時，潛申規諷，謇謇之誠彌切，諤諤之操逾明。

translations.literal: Thus he was able to set his mind on rectifying the age and subtly offer remonstrance; his earnest integrity grew keener, his outspoken integrity shone brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he was able to set his heart on setting the age aright and to offer remonstrance in subtle form; his earnest loyalty grew keener still, his forthright integrity shone the brighter.

sentences.zh: 宜示褒揚，美茲鯁直。

translations.literal: It is fitting to proclaim praise and honor this uncompromising forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to proclaim his merit and honor this uncompromising forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 」賜時服一幅。

translations.literal: He was granted one set of seasonal robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one set of seasonal robes.

sentences.zh: 尋與祝欽明同獻皇后助祭郊祀之議。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he joined Zhu Qinming in submitting a memorial on the Empress's assisting in suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he joined Zhu Qinming in submitting a proposal that the empress assist in the suburban sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，左授括州長史。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era, he was demoted to the left and appointed Chief Administrator of Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun reign, he was transferred to the lesser post of Chief Administrator of Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 開元初，復入為國子司業。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era, he returned to office as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiyuan reign, he returned to office as Vice Director of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 柳沖，蒲州虞鄉人也，隋饒州刺史莊曾孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Chong was a native of Yuxiang in Puzhou, great-grandson of Zhuang, Prefect of Raozhou under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong was from Yuxiang in Puzhou, great-grandson of Zhuang, who had served as Prefect of Raozhou under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 其先仕江左，世居襄陽。

translations.literal: His ancestors served in the lands south of the Yangtze and for generations dwelt in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had served south of the Yangtze and for generations made their home in Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, they returned to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen dynasty fell, the family returned to their native district.

sentences.zh: 父楚賢，大業末，為河北縣長。

translations.literal: His father Chu Xian, at the end of the Daye era, served as Magistrate of Hebei County.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chu Xian, in the final years of the Daye reign, served as Magistrate of Hebei County.

sentences.zh: 時堯君素固守郡城，以拒義師。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Junsu stubbornly held the commandery capital to resist the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yao Junsu stubbornly held the commandery seat, resisting the armies of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 楚賢進說曰：「隋之將亡，天下皆知。

translations.literal: Chu Xian went forward to advise, saying: 'The Sui is about to perish—everyone under Heaven knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Xian went forward to counsel him, saying: 'The Sui is about to perish—everyone under Heaven knows it.

sentences.zh: 唐公名應圖箓，動以信義，豪傑響應，天所贊也！

translations.literal: Lord Tang's name conforms to the charts and registers; he moves with faith and righteousness, and heroes respond—Heaven itself approves!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Tang's name answers to the charts and registers; he acts with faith and righteousness, and heroes rally to him—Heaven itself approves!

sentences.zh: 君子見機而作，不俟終日，轉禍為福，今其時也！

translations.literal: The noble man acts when he sees the moment, not waiting until day's end; to turn calamity into fortune—now is the time!
translations.idiomatic: The noble man acts when he sees the moment, not waiting until day's end; to turn calamity into fortune—now is the time!

sentences.zh: 」君素不從，楚賢潛行歸國。

translations.literal: Junsu would not heed him; Chu Xian secretly departed and returned to the Tang state.
translations.idiomatic: Junsu would not listen; Chu Xian slipped away in secret and returned to the Tang cause.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚悅，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and appointed him Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased and appointed him Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累轉光祿少卿，使突厥存撫李思摩，突厥贈馬百匹及方物，悉拒而不受。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era, he rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Entertainments; sent on a mission to the Turks to console and pacify Li Simo, he refused all the hundred horses and other gifts the Turks offered.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign, he rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Directorate of Imperial Entertainments; sent to the Turks to console and pacify Li Simo, he refused every one of the hundred horses and other gifts they offered.

sentences.zh: 累轉交、桂二州都督，皆有能名。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he served as Military Governor of both Jiao and Gui prefectures, winning repute for ability in each.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he served as Military Governor of Jiao and Gui prefectures, winning repute for ability in both.

sentences.zh: 卒於杭州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 沖博學，尤明世族，名亞路敬淳。

translations.literal: Chong was broadly learned, especially expert in distinguished clans; his reputation was second only to Lu Jingchun.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was broadly learned and especially expert in distinguished clans; his reputation was second only to Lu Jingchun.

sentences.zh: 天授初，為司府主簿，受詔往淮南安撫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianshou era, he served as Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue and was ordered to go to Huainan on a pacification mission.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianshou reign, he served as Senior Clerk of the Ministry of Revenue and was ordered to Huainan on a pacification mission.

sentences.zh: 使還，賜爵河東縣男。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission, he was granted the title Baron of Hedong County.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission, he was granted the title Baron of Hedong County.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷為左散騎常侍，修國史。

translations.literal: During the Jinglong era, he rose to Left Regular Attendant and compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong reign, he rose through successive promotions to Left Regular Attendant and was charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀中太宗命學者撰《氏族志》百卷，以甄別士庶；

translations.literal: Initially, during the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong ordered scholars to compile the Record of Clans in one hundred volumes, to distinguish gentry from commoners;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhenguan reign, Emperor Taizong had ordered scholars to compile the Record of Clans in one hundred volumes, to distinguish gentry from commoners;

sentences.zh: 至是向百年，而諸姓至有興替，沖乃上表請改修氏族。

translations.literal: By this time nearly a century had passed, and among the various surnames there had been rises and falls; Chong thereupon submitted a memorial requesting revision of the clan records.
translations.idiomatic: By then nearly a century had elapsed, and among the great surnames there had been rises and falls; Chong submitted a memorial asking that the clan records be revised.

sentences.zh: 中宗命沖與左僕射魏元忠及史官張錫、徐堅、劉憲等八人，依據《氏族志》，重加修撰。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong ordered Chong, together with Left Vice Director Wei Yuanzhong and the historiographers Zhang Xi, Xu Jian, Liu Xian, and five others—eight men in all—to revise and compile anew based on the Record of Clans.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong ordered Chong, together with Left Vice Director Wei Yuanzhong and the historiographers Zhang Xi, Xu Jian, Liu Xian, and five others—eight men in all—to revise the work afresh on the basis of the Record of Clans.

sentences.zh: 元忠等施功未半，相繼而卒，乃遷為外職。

translations.literal: Before Wei Yuanzhong and the others had completed half the work, they died one after another, and [Chong] was then transferred to an external post.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong and the others had scarcely begun before they died in succession, and Chong was transferred to an external appointment.

sentences.zh: 至先天初，沖始與侍中魏知古、中書侍郎陸象先及徐堅、劉子玄、吳兢等撰成《姓族系錄》二百卷，奏上。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Xiantian era, Chong finally completed, together with Palace Attendant Wei Zhigu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Xiangxian, and Xu Jian, Liu Zixuan, Wu Jing, and others, the Genealogical Records of Surnames and Clans in two hundred volumes, which were submitted to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of the Xiantian reign, Chong at last completed, together with Palace Attendant Wei Zhigu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Lu Xiangxian, and Xu Jian, Liu Zixuan, Wu Jing, and others, the Genealogical Records of Surnames and Clans in two hundred volumes, and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 沖後歷太子詹事、太子賓客、宋王傅、昭文館學士，以老疾致仕。

translations.literal: Later Chong served successively as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Guest of the Heir Apparent, Tutor to the Prince of Song, and academician of the Zhaowen Institute, then retired due to age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later Chong served in succession as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Guest of the Heir Apparent, Tutor to the Prince of Song, and academician of the Zhaowen Institute, then retired on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，又敕沖及著作郎薛南金刊定《系錄》，奏上，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, he was again ordered, together with Director of Compilation Xue Nanjin, to edit and finalize the Genealogical Records; when they submitted the work, he was granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyuan, he was again ordered, together with Director of Compilation Xue Nanjin, to edit and finalize the Genealogical Records; when they submitted the finished work, he was granted one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 五年卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he died.

sentences.zh: 盧粲，幽州范陽人，後魏侍中陽烏五代孫。

translations.literal: Lu Can was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou, fifth-generation descendant of Yang Wu, Attendant-in-Chief of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Can came from Fanyang in Youzhou prefecture, a fifth-generation descendant of Yang Wu, who had served as Attendant-in-Chief under the Later Wei.

sentences.zh: 祖彥卿，撰《後魏紀》二十卷，行於時，官至合肥令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanqing compiled Records of Later Wei in twenty scrolls, which circulated in his time; he reached the office of Magistrate of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanqing compiled the Records of Later Wei in twenty scrolls, which circulated widely in his day; he rose to the post of Magistrate of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 叔父行嘉，亦有學涉，高宗時為雍王記室。

translations.literal: His uncle Xingjia also had learning and breadth; in the time of Emperor Gaozong he served as secretary to the Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Xingjia was likewise a man of scholarly attainments; under Emperor Gaozong he served as secretary to the Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 粲博覽經史，弱冠舉進士。

translations.literal: Can read widely in the classics and histories; at weak-cap age he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Can read widely in the classics and histories, and at twenty he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong, he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong (708) he rose through successive posts to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 時節湣太子初立，韋庶人以非己所生，深加忌嫉，勸中宗下敕令太子卻取衛府封物，每年以供服用。

translations.literal: At that time Crown Prince Jiemin had just been established; Empress Wei, because he was not born of her, deeply resented and envied him, and urged Emperor Zhongzong to issue an edict ordering the crown prince to take back sealed goods from the guard establishment each year for his personal use.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Crown Prince Jiemin had just been installed. Empress Wei, resenting him because he was not her own son, urged Emperor Zhongzong to decree that the crown prince should reclaim sealed goods from the guard bureau each year to supply his personal needs.

sentences.zh: 粲駁奏曰：「皇太子處繼明之重，當主鬯之尊，歲時服用，自可百司供擬。

translations.literal: Can submitted a rebuttal memorial, saying: "The crown prince bears the weight of inheriting the bright succession and holds the dignity of presiding over the sacrificial wine; his seasonal clothing and supplies may naturally be provided by the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Can submitted a rebuttal memorial: "The crown prince bears the weight of inheriting the bright succession and holds the dignity of presiding over the ancestral wine. His seasonal clothing and supplies should naturally be furnished by the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 又據《周官》，諸應用財器，歲終則會，唯王及太子應用物，並不會。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the Rites of Zhou, of all goods and vessels that should be used, at year's end there is an accounting—only goods used by the king and crown prince are not accounted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Rites of Zhou states that of all goods and vessels in use, accounts are rendered at year's end—except for those used by the king and the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 此則儲君之費，鹹與王同。

translations.literal: Thus the heir apparent's expenses are all the same as the king's.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that the heir apparent's expenses are entirely on a par with the king's.

sentences.zh: 今與列國諸侯齊衡入封，豈所謂憲章在昔，垂法將來者也！

translations.literal: To now put him on equal footing with feudal lords of the various states in drawing from fief seals—is this what is meant by 'the constitution rests in the past and the law is handed down to the future'!
translations.idiomatic: To place him now on equal footing with the feudal lords of the realm, drawing from fief seals—is this what is meant by honoring the constitution of old and handing down law to posterity!

sentences.zh: 必謂青宮初啟，服用所資，自當廣支庫物，不可長存籓封。

translations.literal: If one must say the Eastern Palace has just opened and supplies for personal use should naturally be drawn broadly from the treasury stores, one cannot permanently rely on feudal fief seals.
translations.idiomatic: If one insists the Eastern Palace has only just opened and its supplies must be drawn from the treasury at large, that is one thing—but one cannot permanently rely on feudal fief seals.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed his recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 後安樂公主婿武崇訓為節湣太子所殺，特追封為魯王，令司農少卿趙履溫監護葬事。

translations.literal: Later, Wu Chongxun, son-in-law of Princess Anle, was killed by Crown Prince Jiemin; he was specially posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, and Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen was ordered to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Chongxun, Princess Anle's son-in-law, was killed by Crown Prince Jiemin. Chongxun was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, and Zhao Lüwen, Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, was ordered to supervise the burial.

sentences.zh: 履溫諷公主奏請依永泰公主故事，為崇訓造陵。

translations.literal: Lüwen prompted the princess to memorialize requesting that, following the precedent of Princess Yongtai, a ling be built for Chongxun.
translations.idiomatic: Lüwen prompted the princess to memorialize asking that, following the precedent of Princess Yongtai, an imperial tomb be built for Chongxun.

sentences.zh: 詔從其請。

translations.literal: The edict granted her request.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted her request.

sentences.zh: 粲駁奏曰：

translations.literal: Can submitted a rebuttal memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Can submitted a rebuttal memorial:

sentences.zh: 伏尋陵之稱謂，本屬皇王及儲君等。

translations.literal: Upon reflection, the designation 'ling' belongs by origin to emperors, kings, and heir apparents.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reflection, the title ling belongs by origin to emperors, kings, and heir apparents alone.

sentences.zh: 自皇家已來，諸王及公主墓，無稱陵者。

translations.literal: Since our dynasty began, tombs of princes and princesses have never been called ling.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of our house, no tomb of a prince or princess has ever been called a ling.

sentences.zh: 唯永泰公主承恩特葬，事越常塗，不合引以為名。

translations.literal: Only Princess Yongtai, receiving special favor in burial, exceeded the usual path—it is not fitting to cite her as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Only Princess Yongtai, buried by special imperial favor, departed from ordinary practice—it is not fitting to cite her as precedent.

sentences.zh: 《春秋左氏傳》云：「衛孫桓子與齊戰。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "Sun Huanzi of Wei fought with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals says: "Sun Huanzi of Wei fought Qi.

sentences.zh: 衛新築大夫仲叔於奚救孫桓子，桓子以免。

translations.literal: The newly appointed grand officer Zhongsun Yuxi of Wei rescued Sun Huanzi, and Huanzi thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The newly appointed grand officer Zhongsun Yuxi of Wei rescued Sun Huanzi, and Huanzi thereby escaped death.

sentences.zh: 衛人賞之以邑，於奚辭，請曲懸、繁纓以朝，許之。

translations.literal: The people of Wei rewarded him with a fief; Yuxi declined and requested curved suspended bells and rich tassels to wear at court—they granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei wished to reward him with a fief, but Yuxi declined and asked instead for curved suspended bells and rich tassels to wear at court—and they granted it.

sentences.zh: 仲尼聞之，曰：『惜也，不如多與之邑。

translations.literal: Confucius heard of it and said: 'What a pity! Better to have given him more fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Confucius heard of this, he said: 'A pity! Better to have given him more territory.

sentences.zh: 唯名與器，不可以假人。

translations.literal: Titles and ritual emblems may not be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and ritual emblems may not be lent to others.

sentences.zh: 若以假人，與之政也，政亡則國從之。

translations.literal: If you lend them to others, you are lending them government—and when government perishes, the state follows.'
translations.idiomatic: If you lend them to others, you are lending them the government—and when the government is lost, the state follows.'

sentences.zh: 』」聖人知微知章，不可不慎。

translations.literal: The sage knew the subtle and knew the manifest—one cannot but be careful.
translations.idiomatic: The sage knew the subtle and knew the manifest—one cannot but be careful.

sentences.zh: 魯王哀榮之典，誠別承恩；

translations.literal: The rites of honor for Prince of Lu indeed differ as special favor;
translations.idiomatic: The rites of mourning honor for Prince of Lu may indeed reflect special imperial favor;

sentences.zh: 然國之名器，豈可妄假！

translations.literal: yet the state's titles and emblems—how can they be recklessly lent!
translations.idiomatic: but the state's titles and ritual emblems—how can they be recklessly bestowed!

sentences.zh: 又塋兆之稱，不應假永泰公主為名，請比貞觀已來諸王舊例，足得豐厚。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the name for the tomb mound, one should not borrow the name of Princess Yongtai; I ask that we follow the old precedents for princes since the Zhenguan era—those would already be ample.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in naming the tomb one should not borrow the precedent of Princess Yongtai. I ask only that we follow the established precedents for princes since the Zhenguan era—they would already be more than generous.

sentences.zh: 手敕答曰：「安樂公主與永泰公主無異。

translations.literal: A handwritten edict replied: "Princess Anle is no different from Princess Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied in his own hand: "Princess Anle is no different from Princess Yongtai.

sentences.zh: 同穴之義，古今不殊。

translations.literal: The meaning of sharing one tomb is the same in ancient and modern times.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of sharing one tomb is the same in ancient times and today.

sentences.zh: 魯王緣自特為陵制，不煩固執。

translations.literal: Prince of Lu is granted a ling by special order—there is no need to persist obstinately.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lu is granted a ling by special order—there is no need to persist in objection.

sentences.zh: 」粲又奏曰：

translations.literal: Can again submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Can submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞陵之稱謂，施於尊極，不屬王公已下。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the designation 'ling' is applied to the most exalted—it does not belong to kings, dukes, and those below.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has heard that the title ling is reserved for the most exalted—it does not belong to kings, dukes, and those below.

sentences.zh: 且魯王若欲論親等第，則不親於雍王。

translations.literal: Moreover, if Prince of Lu wishes to discuss rank by closeness of kin, he is not closer than the Prince of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if Prince of Lu's rank is judged by closeness of kin, he is not closer than the Prince of Yong.

sentences.zh: 雍王之墓，尚不稱陵，魯王自不可因尚公主而加號。

translations.literal: The tomb of the Prince of Yong still is not called ling—Prince of Lu naturally cannot add the title merely because he married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yong's tomb is still not called a ling—Prince of Lu surely cannot take the title merely because he married a princess.

sentences.zh: 且君之舉事，則載於方冊，或稽之往典，或考自前朝。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a ruler acts, it is recorded in the official chronicles—one examines past canon or looks to former dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when a ruler acts, the deed is recorded in the official chronicles—one consults past canon or examines precedents from earlier reigns.

sentences.zh: 臣歷檢貞觀已來，駙馬墓無得稱陵者。

translations.literal: Your subject has thoroughly searched since the Zhenguan era: no tomb of an imperial son-in-law has been called ling.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has searched every record since the Zhenguan era: not one tomb of an imperial son-in-law has been called a ling.

sentences.zh: 且君人之禮，服絕於傍期，蓋為不獨親其親，不獨子其子。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the rites of a ruler, mourning ends at the next degree of kin—because one does not treat only one's own kin as kin, nor only one's own children as children.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the rites of a ruler, mourning ends at the next degree of kin—for a ruler does not treat only his own kin as kin, nor only his own children as children.

sentences.zh: 陛下以膝下之恩愛，施及其夫，贈赗之儀，哀榮足備，豈得使上下無辨，君臣一貫者哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty, from affection at your knee, extends favor to her husband—the gifts and obsequies are fully ample in grief and honor; how can you make high and low indistinguishable and lord and subject all one!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, from the affection you bear your daughter at your knee, extends favor to her husband—the funeral gifts and obsequies are already ample in grief and honor. How can you make high and low indistinguishable and reduce lord and subject to one level!

sentences.zh: 又安樂公主承兩儀之澤，履福祿之基，指南山以錫年，仰北辰而永庇。

translations.literal: Further, Princess Anle receives the bounty of Heaven and Earth, treads the foundation of fortune and emolument, is granted years like the southern mountain, and eternally sheltered under the north star.
translations.idiomatic: Further, Princess Anle enjoys the bounty of Heaven and Earth, stands upon a foundation of fortune and rank, is granted years like the southern mountain, and rests eternally under the protection of the north star.

sentences.zh: 魯王之葬，車服有章，加等之儀，備有常數，塋兆之稱，不應假永泰公主為名，非所謂垂法將來，作則群辟者也！

translations.literal: In the burial of Prince of Lu, carriage and vestments have their regulations, rites of elevated rank have fixed numbers—the name for the tomb should not borrow that of Princess Yongtai; this is not what is meant by handing down law to the future and establishing a model for all officials!
translations.idiomatic: In Prince of Lu's burial, carriage and vestments already have their proper regulations, and the rites of elevated rank have fixed numbers—the tomb should not borrow the name of Princess Yongtai. This is not what is meant by handing down law to posterity and establishing a model for all officials!

sentences.zh: 帝竟依粲所奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor finally followed what Can had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor at last followed Can's memorial.

sentences.zh: 公主大怒。

translations.literal: The princess was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was furious.

sentences.zh: 粲以忤旨出為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Can, for having defied the imperial will, was sent out as Prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For having defied the imperial will, Can was sent out to serve as Prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 累轉秘書少監。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 開元初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Kaiyuan reign.

sentences.zh: 尹知章，絳州翼城人。

translations.literal: Yin Zhizhang was a man of Yicheng in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhizhang came from Yicheng in Jiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少勤學，嘗夢神人以大鑿開其心，以藥內之，自是日益開朗，盡通諸經精義。

translations.literal: In youth he diligently studied; once he dreamed that a divine man opened his chest with a great chisel and placed medicine inside—thereafter he daily grew clearer in mind and fully mastered the essential meaning of all the classics.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied diligently. Once he dreamed that a divine being opened his chest with a great chisel and placed medicine inside—from that day his mind grew daily clearer, until he had fully mastered the essential meaning of every classic.

sentences.zh: 未幾，而諸師友北面受業焉。

translations.literal: Before long, his teachers and friends all faced north to receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the very men who had been his teachers and peers were facing north to sit at his feet as students.

sentences.zh: 長安中，駙馬都尉武攸暨重其經學，奏授其府定王文學。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an period, the Commandant of Cavalry and Prince Consort Wu Youji valued his classical learning and memorialized that he be appointed Literary Instructor in his household for the Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: While the court was at Chang'an, Prince Consort Wu Youji, Commandant of Cavalry, held his classical scholarship in high regard and memorialized the throne to appoint him Literary Instructor in the household of the Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，轉太常博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era, he was transferred to the post of Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shenlong reign, he was transferred to serve as an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 中宗初即位，建立宗廟，議者欲以涼武昭王為始祖，以備七代之數。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong first took the throne, the ancestral temple was being established, and those debating the matter wished to make the Martial-and-Illustrious King of Liang the founding ancestor, so as to complete the count of seven generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong first ascended the throne and the imperial ancestral temple was being established, some argued that the Martial-and-Illustrious King of Liang should be named founding ancestor, so that the full tally of seven generations might be made up.

sentences.zh: 知章以為武昭遠世，非王業所因，特奏議以為不可。

translations.literal: Zhizhang held that Prince Wu Zhao was too remote in time and was not the source from which royal enterprise had sprung; he submitted a special memorial arguing that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhang argued that Prince Wu Zhao lay too far back in time and was not the line from which the imperial house had risen; he submitted a special memorial declaring the proposal unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 當時竟從知章之議。

translations.literal: At the time the court ultimately followed Zhizhang's opinion.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the court adopted Zhizhang's view.

sentences.zh: 俄拜陸渾令，以公玷棄官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Magistrate of Lu-hun, but because of a public scandal he resigned his office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed magistrate of Lu-hun, but a public scandal forced him to abandon his post.

sentences.zh: 時散騎常侍解琬亦罷職歸田園，與知章共居汝、洛間，以修學為事。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Attendant Xie Wan had also left office and returned to his country estate; he and Zhizhang lived together between the Ru and Luo rivers, devoting themselves to scholarly cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Attendant Xie Wan had likewise left office and retired to the countryside; he and Zhizhang made their home between the Ru and Luo rivers and devoted themselves to study.

sentences.zh: 睿宗初即位，中書令張說薦知章有古人之風，足以鎮雅俗，拜禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong first took the throne, the Chief Minister Zhang Yue recommended Zhizhang as a man with the bearing of the ancients, sufficient to steady refined custom against vulgar fashion, and he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong first ascended the throne, Chief Minister Zhang Yue recommended Zhizhang as a man of ancient bearing, fit to hold refined custom steady against vulgar fashion, and he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 俄轉國子博士。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the post of Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to serve as an Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 後秘書監馬懷素奏引知章就秘書省與學者刊定經史。

translations.literal: Later the Director of the Palace Library Ma Huaisu memorialized that Zhizhang be brought into the Palace Library to join scholars in collating and fixing the Classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Later Director of the Palace Library Ma Huaisu memorialized that Zhizhang be summoned to the Palace Library to join scholars in collating and correcting the Classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 知章雖居吏職，歸家則講授不輟，尤明《易》及莊、老玄言之學，遠近鹹來受業。

translations.literal: Although Zhizhang held an official post, when he returned home he lectured without cease; he was especially versed in the Book of Changes and in the abstruse learning of Zhuangzi and Laozi, and students came from far and near to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held office, Zhizhang never stopped teaching once he was home. He was especially masterful in the Book of Changes and in the abstruse teachings of Zhuangzi and Laozi, and students came from near and far to study under him.

sentences.zh: 其有貧匱者，知章盡其家財以衣食之。

translations.literal: When any among them were poor and destitute, Zhizhang spent his entire household fortune to clothe and feed them.
translations.idiomatic: When any student was poor and destitute, Zhizhang spent his whole household fortune to feed and clothe them.

sentences.zh: 性和厚，喜慍不形於色，未嘗言及家人產業。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle and generous; joy and anger never showed on his face, and he never spoke of his family's property.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle and generous by nature. Neither joy nor anger ever showed on his face, and he never spoke of his family's estate.

sentences.zh: 其子嘗請並市樵米，以備歲時之費，知章曰：「如汝所言，則下人何以取資？

translations.literal: His son once asked that firewood and rice be bought together at market to cover seasonal expenses. Zhizhang said, "As you suggest, how are our servants to make a living?
translations.idiomatic: His son once asked that they buy firewood and rice at market themselves, to cover the year's household expenses. Zhizhang said, "If we do as you propose, how are our servants to earn their keep?

sentences.zh: 吾幸食祿，不宜奪其利也！

translations.literal: I am fortunate to live on my salary — I ought not take away their profit!"
translations.idiomatic: I am fortunate enough to live on my official salary — I should not strip them of their livelihood!"

sentences.zh: 」竟不從。

translations.literal: In the end he did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 開元六年卒，時年五十有余。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Kaiyuan, at a little more than fifty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaiyuan 6, aged a little over fifty.

sentences.zh: 所註《孝經》、《老子》、《莊子》、《韓子》、《管子》、《鬼谷子》，頗行於時。

translations.literal: His commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety, Laozi, Zhuangzi, Han Feizi, Guanzi, and Guiguzi circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His commentaries on the Classic of Filial Piety, Laozi, Zhuangzi, Han Feizi, Guanzi, and Guiguzi were widely read in his day.

sentences.zh: 門人孫季良等立碑於東都國子監之門外，以頌其德。

translations.literal: His disciples Sun Jiliang and others erected a stele outside the gate of the Directorate of Education in the Eastern Capital to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples, Sun Jiliang among them, erected a stele outside the gate of the Eastern Capital's Directorate of Education to honor his virtue.

sentences.zh: 孫季良者，河南偃師人也，一名翌。

translations.literal: Sun Jiliang was a native of Yanshi in Henan; he also went by the name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jiliang was a native of Yanshi in Henan and also went by the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 開元中，為左拾遺、集賢院直學士。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era he served as Left Reminder and Academician-in-Attendance at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he served as Left Reminder and Academician-in-Attendance at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 撰《正聲詩集》三卷，行於代。

translations.literal: He compiled Correct Sounds: A Poetry Collection in three fascicles, which circulated in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Correct Sounds: A Poetry Collection in three fascicles, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 徐岱，字處仁，蘇州嘉興人也。

translations.literal: Xu Dai, courtesy name Churen, was a native of Jiaxing in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dai, courtesy name Churen, came from Jiaxing in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 家世以農為業。

translations.literal: His family for generations had made its living by farming.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had lived by farming.

sentences.zh: 岱好學，六籍諸子，悉所探究，問無不通，難莫能詘。

translations.literal: Dai loved learning; the Six Classics and the various masters he investigated thoroughly. No question stumped him, and no challenge could defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Dai loved learning and had explored the Six Classics and the various masters in depth. No question could stump him, and no challenge could best him.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，轉運使劉晏表薦之，授校書郎。

translations.literal: During the Dali era, the Transport Commissioner Liu Yan memorialized recommending him, and he was appointed Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali reign, Transport Commissioner Liu Yan recommended him by memorial, and he was appointed Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李棲筠厚遇之，敕故所居為復禮鄉。

translations.literal: The Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun treated him with great favor and had his former residence designated Fuli Village by imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Qiyun treated him with exceptional favor and obtained an imperial decree naming his former home Fuli Village.

sentences.zh: 尋為朝廷推援，改河南府偃師縣尉。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted by the court and transferred to the post of Assistant Magistrate of Yanshi County in Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court advanced him to the post of assistant magistrate of Yanshi County in Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中年，禮儀使蔣鎮特薦為太常博士，掌禮儀。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era, the Commissioner of Ritual Jiang Zhen specially recommended him as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, in charge of ritual affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianzhong reign, Commissioner of Ritual Jiang Zhen specially recommended him for appointment as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with charge of ritual affairs.

sentences.zh: 從幸奉天、興元，改膳部員外郎兼博士。

translations.literal: When he followed the emperor on the journeys to Fengtian and Xingyuan, he was made Vice Director in the Foods Section while retaining his post as Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When he accompanied the emperor to Fengtian and Xingyuan, he was made Vice Director in the Foods Section while continuing to serve as Erudite.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，遷水部郎中，充皇太子及舒王已下侍讀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he was promoted to Director in the Waterways Section and appointed Reader to the Crown Prince and to Prince Shu and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan reign he was promoted to Director in the Waterways Section and appointed Reader to the Crown Prince and to Prince Shu and the princes below him.

sentences.zh: 尋改司封郎中，擢拜給事中，加兼史館修撰，並依舊侍讀。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Director in the Section of Enfeoffments, then elevated and appointed Censor-in-Chief, with the additional appointment of Compiler in the Historiography Institute, while continuing as Reader as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Director in the Section of Enfeoffments, then elevated to Censor-in-Chief and additionally appointed Compiler in the Historiography Institute, all while continuing as Reader.

sentences.zh: 承兩宮恩顧，時無與比。

translations.literal: He enjoyed the favor and regard of both palaces, and at the time none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed the favor of both the emperor and the empress dowager, and for a time none could rival him.

sentences.zh: 而謹慎過甚，未嘗泄禁中語，亦不談人之短。

translations.literal: Yet he was excessively cautious: he never leaked words from within the palace, nor did he speak of others' faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was almost excessively cautious — he never breathed a word of palace affairs, nor did he speak ill of others.

sentences.zh: 婚嫁甥侄之孤遺者，時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: He saw to the marriages of orphaned nephews and nieces, and people of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged marriages for orphaned nephews and nieces, and people of the time praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 然吝嗇頗甚，倉庫管鑰，皆自執掌，獲譏於時。

translations.literal: Yet he was also quite miserly; the keys to the storerooms he kept in his own hands, and for this he drew criticism in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was also deeply miserly — he kept the keys to the storerooms in his own hands, and for this he was widely criticized.

sentences.zh: 卒，時年五十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 上嘆惜之，賻以帛絹。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in regret and granted silks for his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed in regret and granted silks for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 皇太子又遺絹一百疋，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince also sent one hundred bolts of silk and had him posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince also sent one hundred bolts of silk and had him posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 蘇弁，字元容，京兆武功人。

translations.literal: Su Bian, courtesy name Yuanrong, was a native of Wugong in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Su Bian, courtesy name Yuanrong, came from Wugong in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾叔祖良嗣，天後朝宰相，國史有傳。

translations.literal: His grand-uncle Liangsi had been a chancellor in the reign of the Empress of Heaven and has a biography in the dynastic history.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-uncle Liangsi had served as chancellor under the Empress of Heaven and has a biography in the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 弁少有文學，舉進士，授秘書省正字，轉奉天主簿。

translations.literal: Bian in his youth had literary talent; he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Corrector in the Palace Library, then transferred to Chief Clerk of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Bian showed literary talent from youth. He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Corrector in the Palace Library, and was later transferred to chief clerk of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，德宗倉卒出幸，縣令杜正元上府計事；

translations.literal: During the rebellion of Zhu Ci, Emperor Dezong fled the capital in haste, and the magistrate Du Zhengyuan went up to the prefectural seat to discuss affairs;
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Emperor Dezong fled the capital in haste. The county magistrate Du Zhengyuan went up to the prefectural seat to discuss affairs;

sentences.zh: 聞大駕至，官吏惶恐，皆欲奔竄山谷。

translations.literal: when word came that the imperial carriage was approaching, the officials were terrified and all wished to flee into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the imperial carriage was approaching, the officials were terrified and all wanted to flee into the hills.

sentences.zh: 弁諭之曰：「君上避狄，臣下當伏難死節。

translations.literal: Bian admonished them, saying, "When the sovereign flees barbarian invasion, his ministers ought to meet disaster and die with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Bian admonished them, saying, "When the sovereign flees barbarian invasion, his ministers ought to meet disaster and die with honor.

sentences.zh: 昔肅宗幸靈武，至新平、安定，二太守皆潛遁，帝命斬之以徇，諸君知其事乎！

translations.literal: In former times, when Emperor Suzong went to Lingwu, at Xinping and Anding both prefects secretly fled; the emperor ordered them beheaded as a warning. Do you gentlemen know this affair?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong withdrew to Lingwu, the prefects of Xinping and Anding both fled in secret, and the emperor had them beheaded as a warning to all. Do you know this story?"

sentences.zh: 」眾心乃安。

translations.literal: The hearts of the crowd were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Only then were the men's hearts steadied.

sentences.zh: 及車駕至，迎扈儲備無闕。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage arrived, they received and escorted it, and the stores and provisions were complete without lack.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage arrived, they received and escorted it, and the stores and provisions were ready without the slightest shortfall.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，就加試大理司直。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong commended him and on the spot additionally appointed him Acting Director in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong commended him and on the spot appointed him Acting Director in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 賊平，拜監察御史，歷三院，累轉倉部郎中。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Investigating Censor, served in all three bureaus, and was repeatedly transferred until he became Director in the Granaries Section.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he was appointed Investigating Censor. He served in all three censorate bureaus in turn and rose by successive transfer to Director in the Granaries Section.

sentences.zh: 仍判度支案。

translations.literal: He continued to adjudicate fiscal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He also continued to oversee cases in the Department of Public Revenue.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡卒，德宗聞其才，特開延英，面賜金紫。

translations.literal: When Pei Yanling died, Dezong heard of his talent, specially convened Yingying Hall, and in person bestowed the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yanling died, Emperor Dezong heard of Bian's talent, convened a special audience in Yingying Hall, and personally bestowed on him the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 授度支郎中，副知度支事，仍命立於正郎之首。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director in the Revenue Section, made assistant overseer of revenue affairs, and was also ordered to stand at the head of the regular directors.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director in the Revenue Section and made assistant overseer of revenue affairs, and was also ordered to take the foremost place among the regular directors.

sentences.zh: 副知之號，自弁始也。

translations.literal: The title of assistant overseer began with Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The title of assistant overseer dates from Bian.

sentences.zh: 承延齡之後，以寬簡代煩虐，人甚稱之。

translations.literal: Succeeding after Yanling, he replaced vexatious harshness with leniency and simplicity, and people greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Succeeding Pei Yanling, he replaced vexatious severity with a lenient and straightforward manner, and the people greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎，依前判度支，改太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, continued as before to oversee revenue, and was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, continued as before to oversee the Revenue Section, and was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弁初入朝，班位失序，殿中侍御史鄒儒立對仗彈之。

translations.literal: When Bian first entered court audience, his place in the ranks was out of order, and Palace Censor Zou Ruli impeached him at the formal session.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian first attended court, he took the wrong place in the ranks, and Palace Censor Zou Ruli impeached him at the formal session.

sentences.zh: 弁於金吾待罪數刻，特釋放。

translations.literal: Bian waited in disgrace at the Golden Guard for several quarters of an hour, then was specially released.
translations.idiomatic: Bian waited for judgment at the Golden Guard office for some time, then was specially released.

sentences.zh: 舊制，太子詹事班次太常、宗正卿已下。

translations.literal: By old regulation, the Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent ranked below the Ministers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, the Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent ranked below the Ministers of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，御史中丞竇參敘定班，移詹事在河南、太原尹之下。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, Censor-in-Chief Dou Can ordered the ranks and moved the Grand Tutor below the Prefects of Henan and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3, Censor-in-Chief Dou Can revised the court ranks and placed the Grand Tutor below the Prefects of Henan and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 弁乃引舊班制立。

translations.literal: Bian then took his place according to the old rank order.
translations.idiomatic: Bian then took his place according to the old rank order.

sentences.zh: 臺官詰之，仍紿云：「自己白宰相，請依舊。

translations.literal: The censorial officials questioned him, and he still deceived them, saying, "I told the chancellor myself and asked to follow the old order.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials questioned him, but he lied, saying, "I spoke to the chancellor myself and asked to follow the old order.

sentences.zh: 」故為儒立彈之。

translations.literal: " Therefore Ruli impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: " That is why Ruli impeached him.

sentences.zh: 旋坐給長武城軍糧朽敗，貶河州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, because the grain supplied to the Changwu garrison army had rotted, he was demoted to Registrar of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was convicted of having supplied rotten grain to the army at Changwu Fort and was demoted to Registrar of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 當德宗時，朝臣受譴，少蒙再錄，至晚年尤甚。

translations.literal: During Dezong's reign, court officials who were punished rarely received a second appointment, and this was especially so in his later years.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Dezong, punished officials were rarely given a second chance at office — and in his later years this was especially true.

sentences.zh: 唯弁與韓臯得起為刺史，授滁州，轉杭州。

translations.literal: Only Bian and Han Gao among them were restored as prefects; he was given Chuzhou and then transferred to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Only Bian and Han Gao were restored to prefectural office; Bian was assigned to Chuzhou and later transferred to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弁與兄冕、袞，皆以友弟、儒學稱。

translations.literal: Bian, together with his elder brothers Mian and Gun, were all famed for brotherly friendship and Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Bian and his elder brothers Mian and Gun were all renowned for their fraternal bond and their learning in the Confucian classics.

sentences.zh: 冕，纘國朝政事，撰《會要》四十卷，行於時。

translations.literal: Mian compiled the court affairs of the dynasty and wrote Institutional Essentials in forty fascicles, which circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Mian compiled the affairs of the dynasty's court and wrote Institutional Essentials in forty fascicles, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 弁聚書至二萬卷，皆手自刊校，至今言蘇氏書，次於集賢秘閣焉。

translations.literal: Bian gathered books to the number of twenty thousand fascicles, all personally collated and corrected by his own hand; even to this day, when men speak of the Su family's books, they rank second only to the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Bian amassed a library of twenty thousand fascicles, every volume collated by his own hand; even now, when scholars speak of the Su family's collection, they rank it second only to the Hall of Assembled Worthies and the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 21, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 袞自贊善大夫貶永州司戶參軍，敕：「蘇袞貶官，本緣弟連坐。

translations.literal: Gun, who had been demoted from Supporter-of-Goodness Grandee to Registrar of Yongzhou, received an edict: "Su Gun's demotion originally arose from his younger brother's implication.
translations.idiomatic: Gun had been demoted from Supporter-of-Goodness Grandee to Registrar of Yongzhou when an edict declared: "Su Gun's demotion arose from implication in his younger brother's crime.

sentences.zh: 矜其年暮，加以疾患，宜令所在勒回，任歸私第。

translations.literal: Pitying his advanced age and the added burden of illness, he should be ordered turned back where he is and allowed to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying his advanced age and illness, let the authorities where he is order him to turn back and allow him to retire to his home.

sentences.zh: 」袞年且七十，兩目無見已逾年。

translations.literal: " Gun was nearly seventy, and both eyes had been sightless for more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: " Gun was nearly seventy, and had been blind in both eyes for more than a year.

sentences.zh: 以弁之故，竟未停官。

translations.literal: Because of Bian's affair, in the end he had not been removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: As long as Bian remained in favor, Gun was never actually dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 及貶，上聞之哀憫，故許還家。

translations.literal: When he was demoted, the emperor heard of it and felt pity, and therefore permitted him to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When the demotion took effect, the emperor heard of his plight and took pity, and allowed him to return home.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 初，冕既坐弁貶官，或有人言冕才學，上悔不早知。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mian had already been demoted because of Bian; someone spoke of Mian's talent and learning, and the emperor regretted not having known sooner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Mian had been demoted because of Bian; when someone spoke of Mian's talent and learning, the emperor regretted not having known it sooner.

sentences.zh: 業已貶出，又復還袞，難於再追冕，乃止。

translations.literal: Mian had already been demoted and sent away, and Gun had again been restored; it was awkward to recall Mian as well, and so the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had already been demoted and sent away, and Gun had already been recalled; recalling Mian as well would have been awkward, and so the emperor let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 時執誼得幸，順帝寢疾，與王叔文等竊弄權柄。

translations.literal: At that time Zhíyì had gained favor; Emperor Shun lay ill in bed, and together with Wang Shuwen and others he secretly wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Shuwen had won the emperor's favor. When Emperor Shun fell ill, he and his faction secretly usurped the powers of state.

sentences.zh: 上在春宮，執誼懼，質已用事，故令質入侍，而潛伺上意，因用解。

translations.literal: The crown prince was in the Eastern Palace; Shuwen was afraid because Lu Zhi already held power, and therefore had Zhi enter to attend him, while secretly watching the crown prince's intent, intending to use this to resolve the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince resided in the Eastern Palace. Shuwen feared that Lu Zhi already wielded influence there, and so sent Zhi in to attend him while secretly probing the crown prince's mind, hoping thereby to find a solution.

sentences.zh: 及質發言，上果怒曰：「陛下令先生與寡人講義，何得言他？

translations.literal: When Zhi spoke, the crown prince indeed grew angry and said, "His Majesty ordered the Master to discuss the classics with me — how dare you speak of other matters?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi began to speak, the crown prince flew into a rage. "His Majesty ordered you, Master, to expound the classics with me — what business have you speaking of anything else?

sentences.zh: 」質惶懼而出。

translations.literal: " Zhi left in terror.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhi withdrew in fear and dismay.

sentences.zh: 未幾病卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 質著《集註春秋》二十卷，《類禮》二十卷，《君臣圖翼》二十五卷，並行於代。

translations.literal: Zhi authored Collected Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals in twenty fascicles, Categorized Rites in twenty fascicles, and Chart and Wings of Ruler and Subject in twenty-five fascicles, all of which circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wrote Collected Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals in twenty fascicles, Categorized Rites in twenty fascicles, and Chart and Wings of Ruler and Subject in twenty-five fascicles, all widely circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenyuan 21.

sentences.zh: 馮伉，本魏州元城人。

translations.literal: Feng Kang was originally a native of Yuancheng in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Kang was originally from Yuancheng in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父玠，後家於京兆。

translations.literal: His father Jie later established the family in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie later settled the family in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少有經學。

translations.literal: In youth he had learning in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was versed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，登《五經》秀才科，授秘書郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era, he passed the Five Classics Cultivated Talent examination and was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dali reign he passed the Five Classics Cultivated Talent examination and was appointed Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 建中四年，又登博學《三史》科。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhong, he again passed the Erudite Examination in the Three Histories.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 4 (783) he passed the Erudite Examination in the Three Histories as well.

sentences.zh: 三遷尚書膳部員外郎，充睦王已下侍讀。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Board of Rites, Department of Provisions, and served as tutor to the Prince of Mu and the princes below him.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted three times, he was appointed Vice Director of the Board of Rites, Department of Provisions, and served as tutor to the Prince of Mu and the junior princes.

sentences.zh: 澤潞節度使李抱真卒，為吊贈使，抱真男遺伉帛數百匹，不納。

translations.literal: When Li Baozhen, Military Governor of Zelu, died, Kang was made envoy to offer condolences and posthumous honors; Baozhen's son sent Kang several hundred bolts of silk, which he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Baozhen, military governor of Zelu, died, Kang was dispatched as envoy to offer condolences and posthumous honors. Baozhen's son sent him several hundred bolts of silk; he refused them.

sentences.zh: 又專送至京，伉因表奏，固請不受。

translations.literal: They were again sent separately to the capital; Kang thereupon submitted a memorial firmly requesting not to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: The gifts were sent again, this time straight to the capital. Kang submitted a memorial insisting that he would not take them.

sentences.zh: 屬醴泉闕縣令，宰臣進人名，帝意不可，謂宰臣曰：「前使澤潞不受財帛者，此人必有清政，可以授之。

translations.literal: It happened that Liquan lacked a county magistrate; the chief ministers submitted names, but the emperor was not satisfied and told the chief ministers: "The man who earlier went as envoy to Zelu and refused silk and cloth—this man must surely govern with integrity and may be given the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the magistracy of Liquan fell vacant, the chief ministers put forward candidates, but the emperor was not pleased. He told them: "The man who went to Zelu as envoy and refused silk and cloth—he must govern with clean hands. Give him the post.

sentences.zh: 」遂改醴泉令。

translations.literal: " He was thereupon transferred to be magistrate of Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: " Kang was accordingly appointed magistrate of Liquan.

sentences.zh: 縣中百姓多猾，為著《諭蒙》十四篇，大略指明忠孝仁義，勸學務農，每鄉給一卷，俾其傳習。

translations.literal: Many of the common people in the county were crafty; he therefore composed fourteen chapters of Instruction for the Untaught, broadly setting forth loyalty, filial piety, benevolence, and righteousness, urging study and urging agriculture; one scroll was given to each township, so that they might transmit and practice it.
translations.idiomatic: The common people of the county were often shrewd and difficult. He therefore wrote Instruction for the Untaught in fourteen chapters, setting out loyalty, filial piety, benevolence, and righteousness and urging learning and farming. One copy went to each township, that the people might study and pass it on.

sentences.zh: 在縣七年，韋渠牟薦為給事中，充皇太子及諸王侍讀。

translations.literal: After seven years in the county, Wei Qumou recommended him as Supervising Secretary, and he served as tutor to the crown prince and the princes.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years as magistrate, Wei Qumou recommended him for Supervising Secretary, and he served as tutor to the crown prince and the princes.

sentences.zh: 召見於別殿，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience in a separate hall and granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience in a side hall and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 著《三傳異同》三卷。

translations.literal: He authored Variations and Agreements among the Three Commentaries in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Variations and Agreements among the Three Commentaries in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，拜尚書兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, Kang was appointed Vice Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong ascended the throne, Kang was appointed Vice Minister of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 改國子祭酒，為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and made Prefect of Tong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and appointed prefect of Tong.

sentences.zh: 入拜左散騎常侍，復領太學。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, again heading the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was appointed Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and again put in charge of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 元和四年卒，年六十六，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe he died, aged sixty-six; posthumously he was made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanhe 4 (809), aged sixty-six, and was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子藥，進士擢第，又登制科，仕至尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Yao passed the jinshi examination, also passed a special examination, and in office rose to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yao passed the jinshi examination and a special examination as well, rising in office to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 韋表微，始舉進士登第，累佐籓府。

translations.literal: Wei Biaowei first passed the jinshi examination and successively served as staff in frontier administrations.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Biaowei first passed the jinshi examination and served in succession on the staffs of regional administrations.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 15 (820) he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以本官充翰林學士。

translations.literal: After a year, in his existing office he was made Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Hanlin Academician while retaining his censor's post.

sentences.zh: 遷左補闕、庫部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Reminder, Vice Director of the Board of Finance, Treasuries Bureau, and Drafting Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Reminder, Vice Director of the Board of Finance, Treasuries Bureau, with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 滿歲，擢遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When his year was complete, he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After a full year in office he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 俄拜戶部侍郎，職並如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, his duties remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue, his other duties unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時自長慶、寶歷，國家比有變故，凡在翰林，遷擢例無滿歲，由是表微自監察，六七年間，秩正貳卿，命服金紫，承遇恩渥，盛於一時。

translations.literal: At that time, from the Changqing and Baoli reigns onward the state had lately suffered repeated upheavals; for all who served in the Hanlin Academy, promotion by precedent did not wait for a full year—thus Biaowei, from Investigating Censor, within six or seven years held the proper rank of a vice minister, was granted the gold seal and purple robe, received imperial favor thick upon him, and flourished beyond any man of his day.
translations.idiomatic: From the Changqing and Baoli reigns on, the court had been shaken by one crisis after another. Hanlin academicians were by custom promoted before a full year in post—and so Biaowei, starting as Investigating Censor, within six or seven years held a vice minister's proper rank, wore the gold seal and purple robe, and enjoyed imperial favor surpassing any man of his time.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 表微少時，克苦自立。

translations.literal: In youth Biaowei endured hardship and built himself up through his own effort.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Biaowei bore hardship and raised himself by his own labor.

sentences.zh: 著《九經師授譜》一卷，《春秋三傳總例》二十卷。

translations.literal: He authored Genealogies of Masters of the Nine Classics in one scroll and General Principles of the Three Commentaries to the Spring and Autumn Annals in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Genealogies of Masters of the Nine Classics in one scroll and General Principles of the Three Commentaries to the Spring and Autumn Annals in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子蟾，進士登第，咸通末，為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His son Chan passed the jinshi examination; at the end of the Xiantong era he served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chan passed the jinshi examination and, in the late Xiantong period, served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 許康佐，父審。

translations.literal: Xu Kangzuo—his father was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kangzuo's father was Shen.

sentences.zh: 康佐登進士第，又登宏詞科。

translations.literal: Kangzuo passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Hongci examination.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzuo passed the jinshi examination and the Hongci examination as well.

sentences.zh: 以家貧母老，求為知院官，人或怪之，笑而不答。

translations.literal: Because his family was poor and his mother old, he sought appointment as an academy officer; some found this strange, but he smiled and would not answer.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and his mother aged, so he sought a post as an academy officer. Some thought it odd; he only smiled and would not explain.

sentences.zh: 及母亡，服除，不就侯府之辟，君子始知其不擇祿養親之誌也，故名益重。

translations.literal: When his mother died and mourning was complete, he did not accept appointment from a marquis's household; gentlemen of worth then first understood his resolve not to choose salary over caring for his parent, and his name grew ever weightier.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died and his mourning was done, he declined appointment from a marquis's household. Only then did men of worth see that he had refused to trade salary for filial duty—and his reputation grew all the heavier.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史，轉職方員外郎，累遷至駕部郎中，充翰林侍講學士，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor, then Vice Director of the Board of War, Bureau of Appointments; he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Board of War, Bureau of Transport, served as Hanlin Lecturing Academician, and was also granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Censor, then Vice Director of the Board of War, Bureau of Appointments, and in time rose to Director of the Board of War, Bureau of Transport. He served as Hanlin Lecturing Academician and was granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 歷諫議大夫、中書舍人，皆在內庭。

translations.literal: He served as Remonstrance and Review Official and Secretariat Drafter—all within the inner court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Remonstrance and Review Official and Secretariat Drafter, always within the inner court.

sentences.zh: 為戶部侍郎，以疾解職。

translations.literal: He became Vice Minister of Revenue and resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Minister of Revenue but resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 除兵部侍郎，轉禮部尚。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of War and transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of War and then transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-two; posthumously he was made Minister of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two and was posthumously honored as Minister of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 撰《九鼎記》四卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Record of the Nine Cauldrons in four scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Record of the Nine Cauldrons in four scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟堯佐、元佐，堯佐子道敏，並登進士第，歷官清顯。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Yaozuo and Yuanzuo, and Yaozuo's son Daomin, all passed the jinshi examination and held distinguished, unsullied offices.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Yaozuo and Yuanzuo, and Yaozuo's son Daomin, all passed the jinshi examination and rose to clean, eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：積學成功，開談辨治。

translations.literal: Encomium: Accumulated learning achieves success; open discourse distinguishes good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Through accumulated learning they achieved mastery; in open discourse they clarified what makes governance sound.

sentences.zh: 儒道玄機，聖人雅旨。

translations.literal: The profound mechanism of the Confucian Way, the elegant intent of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: They held the deep workings of the Confucian Way and the sages' refined purpose.

sentences.zh: 出必由戶，行跡其軌。

translations.literal: One goes out only through the door; one's steps follow the track.
translations.idiomatic: They entered and left only by the proper door; their steps kept to the path.

sentences.zh: 邈有其人，光乎信史。

translations.literal: Far off there are such men—they shine in the faithful histories.
translations.idiomatic: Such men are not near at hand—and yet they shine in the faithful histories.
